Sita pours a jug into an empty 1 L bottle. The bottle overflows. What does this tell her?
options: The jug held more than 1 L
The jug held less than 1 L
quiz.explain: Overflowing means there was more water than the bottle could hold.

quiz.q: Which holds less than 1 litre?
quiz.explain: A tea glass holds about 200 ml.
quiz.mistake: Has no sense of a litre

quiz.q: How many 50 ml cups fill a 1 L bottle?
Ali fills a 1 L bottle using one 500 ml mug and some 250 ml cups. How many 250 ml cups?
Which container most likely holds about 1 litre?
quiz.explain: A big water bottle usually holds 1 litre.
quiz.mistake: Picks something too big or small

teach.ask: Gappu has only 250 ml cups and wants to fill a 1 litre bottle. How many cups? Explain.
teach.praise: 1000 ÷ 250 = 4 cups! The bottle is full.
teach.nudge: How many ml are in 1 litre, and how many 250s fit?

learn.hook: How many 100 ml cups fill half a litre? And 750 ml? And 800 ml?
points: Number of small measures = amount ÷ size of the measure: 800 ml ÷ 100 ml = 8.
To fill an order of 1 L with different bottles: 500 ml + 250 ml + 250 ml = 1000 ml.

example.q: How many 250 ml glasses fill a 750 ml jug?

learn.reallife: A juice shop may sell 250 ml glasses from a 750 ml jug, or fill a 1 litre order with 500 ml and 250 ml bottles.

quiz.q: How many 100 ml cups fill half a litre?
quiz.mistake: Thinks half a litre is 50 ml

quiz.q: How many 250 ml glasses fill a 750 ml jug?
How many 100 ml cups are in 800 ml?
An order is for 1 L of oil. The shop has 500 ml and 250 ml bottles. Which set fills the order exactly?
How many 50 ml cups make 1/2 L?
How many 250 ml bottles are needed for 3/4 L?
An order of 1 L is filled with one 500 ml bottle and some 100 ml bottles. How many 100 ml bottles?
A jug holds 800 ml. How many 200 ml glasses can it fill?

teach.ask: Gappu has a 750 ml jug of lassi and 250 ml glasses. How many friends can Gappu serve?
teach.praise: 750 ÷ 250 = 3 glasses. Three happy friends!
teach.nudge: How many 250s fit into 750?

topics.title: Small measures: dosing cups and droppers

learn.hook: Cough syrup comes with a tiny 10 ml cup. Eye drops come one drop at a time. Small measures matter!
points: A dosing cup often holds 10 ml. 10 cups = 100 ml. 100 cups = 1 L.
25 cups of 10 ml make 250 ml. 50 cups make 500 ml.
A 1 ml dropper takes 10 fills to make 10 ml. A teaspoon holds about 5 ml, so 5 dropper-fulls.
Typical amounts: eye drops 1 or 2 drops, syrup 5 to 10 ml, a spoon of honey about 15 ml, cooking oil a few spoons (30 to 50 ml).

example.q: How many 10 ml dosing cups make 250 ml?

learn.reallife: Doctors write '5 ml twice a day' on a prescription. Using the right measure keeps us safe!

games.title: Typical amount used at one time

quiz.q: How many 10 ml dosing cups make 100 ml?
How many 10 ml cups make 500 ml?
How many 10 ml cups make 1 litre?
A dropper holds 1 ml. How many dropper-fulls make 10 ml?
A teaspoon holds about 5 ml. How many 1 ml dropper-fulls fill it?
Which is a sensible amount of cough syrup for one dose?
quiz.explain: A dose of syrup is usually 5 to 10 ml.
quiz.mistake: Has no sense of small measures

quiz.q: How many drops of eye medicine are usually put at one time?
quiz.explain: Eye drops are used one or two drops at a time.

quiz.q: A syrup bottle has 100 ml. One dose is 10 ml. How many doses are in the bottle?

teach.ask: Gappu has a 10 ml cup and needs 250 ml of rose syrup for a party drink. How many cups should Gappu pour?
teach.praise: 250 ÷ 10 = 25 cups. Party drink ready!
teach.nudge: How many 10s are there in 250?

topics.title: Market survey: by weight or by volume?

learn.hook: In a shop, rice is sold in kg but oil is sold in litres. Why the difference?
points: Solids like rice, dal, sugar, vegetables and fruit are sold by weight (g or kg).
Liquids like milk, oil, juice and water are sold by volume (ml or L).
Common weight packs: 100 g, 200 g, 250 g, 500 g, 1 kg, 5 kg.
Common liquid packs: 200 ml, 500 ml, 1 L, 2 L, 5 L.
Read the label: it tells how much is inside the pack.

example.q: Which unit is printed on a milk packet and which on a sugar packet?
steps: Milk is a liquid: sold by volume, so ml or L.
Sugar is a solid: sold by weight, so g or kg.
example.answer: Milk in ml or L; sugar in g or kg

learn.reallife: Go with your family to a kirana shop and read the labels: '500 g biscuits', '1 L oil', '200 ml juice'!

games.title: Sold by weight or by volume?
Pack sizes
items: Biscuits often come in 100 g or 200 g packs.
Small snack packs are in grams.
Milk is sold in kg packets.
Milk is a liquid, sold in ml or litres.
Oil comes in 1 L and 5 L cans.
Rice is sold by weight, in kg.
A 500 ml bottle holds half a litre.

quiz.q: Which item is sold by volume?
quiz.explain: Oil is a liquid, so it is sold in ml or L.

quiz.q: Which item is sold by weight?
quiz.explain: Dal is a solid, sold in g or kg.

quiz.q: Which is a common pack size for biscuits?
quiz.explain: Biscuit packs are small, like 100 g or 200 g.
quiz.mistake: Uses a liquid or very big unit

quiz.q: A label says '2 L'. What could the pack be?
quiz.explain: L is for liquids, like a cold drink.
quiz.mistake: Does not link L to liquids

quiz.q: Riya's survey lists: rice 5 kg, milk 1 L, oil 1 L, sugar 1 kg, juice 200 ml. How many items are sold by volume?
quiz.explain: Milk, oil and juice: 3 items.

quiz.q: Which unit belongs on a shampoo bottle?
quiz.explain: Shampoo is a liquid, measured in ml.
quiz.mistake: Picks a weight or length unit

quiz.q: A 500 g packet of salt and a 500 ml bottle of water. Which statement is true?
options: Salt is sold by weight; water by volume
quiz.explain: g is for weight and ml is for volume.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a common size for milk packets?
quiz.explain: Milk packets are small or medium, not 50 L.
quiz.mistake: Picks a sensible size by mistake

teach.ask: Gappu is confused why rice is in kg and milk is in litres. Explain to Gappu.
teach.praise: Solids are weighed and liquids are measured by volume. Shopping makes sense now!
teach.nudge: Which kinds of things are sold by weight and which by volume?

topics.title: How much water do we use?

learn.hook: A bucket bath, a glass of water, watering plants... Every activity uses water. Which uses the most?
points: A child drinks about 1 to 2 litres of water a day. A cow drinks about 50 litres or more.
A bucket bath uses about 15 to 20 litres. A shower can use much more.
Washing clothes, cleaning floors and watering plants use many litres too.
To compare activities, put the estimated litres in a table and find the most and the least.

example.q: Estimates: bath 20 L, brushing teeth 2 L, washing clothes 40 L, drinking 2 L. Which uses the most and which the least?
steps: Least: brushing teeth and drinking, 2 L each.
example.answer: Most: washing clothes; least: brushing and drinking

learn.reallife: Many villages and cities face water shortage in summer. Knowing how much we use helps us save it.

quiz.q: About how much water does a child drink in a day?
quiz.explain: A child drinks around 6 to 8 glasses, about 1 to 2 litres.
quiz.mistake: Picks a very big or very small amount

quiz.q: Which uses the most water?
quiz.explain: Washing clothes needs many buckets of water.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the amount used

quiz.q: Estimates: bath 20 L, cooking 10 L, cleaning 15 L, drinking 8 L for a family. Which uses the least?
quiz.explain: 8 L is the smallest.

quiz.q: In that table, how much more water is used for the bath than for cooking?
A family of 4 each takes a 20 L bucket bath daily. How much water for baths in a day?
Which is a sensible amount for a cow to drink in a day?
quiz.explain: A cow is big and drinks many litres, about 50 L or more.
quiz.mistake: Uses ml for a large amount

quiz.q: Mohan waters plants with a 10 L bucket, 3 times. How much water does he use?
A family drinks 8 L, cooks with 12 L and washes dishes with 25 L. What is the total?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know which home activity uses the most water. How can Gappu find out?
teach.praise: I listed each activity's litres in a table. Washing clothes uses the most!
teach.nudge: How can you measure or estimate each activity and compare them?

learn.hook: Drip, drip, drip... A leaking tap can waste a whole bucket of water every day!
points: Put a mug under a leaking tap for one hour and measure the water collected.
Daily loss = loss in 1 hour × 24 hours. Weekly loss = daily loss × 7.
If a tap leaks 500 ml in an hour, it wastes 24 × 500 = 12,000 ml = 12 L a day, and 84 L a week.
Ways to save water: fix leaks, close the tap while brushing, use a bucket not a shower, reuse water from washing vegetables for plants.

example.q: A tap leaks 250 ml in one hour. How much does it waste in one day (24 hours)?

learn.reallife: Some schools hold 'Save Water' drives where children check every tap and report leaks.

games.title: Saves water or wastes water?
items: Using a bucket for a bath
Washing a car with a running hose

quiz.q: A tap leaks 500 ml in 1 hour. How much does it leak in 24 hours?
A tap wastes 12 L a day. How much does it waste in a week?
A tap fills a 100 ml cup in 1 hour from drips. How many ml in 10 hours?
Which is the best way to save water?
options: Turn off the tap while brushing
Let the tap run while soaping hands
Wash the car with a running hose
quiz.explain: Turning the tap off when not in use saves many litres.
quiz.mistake: Does not see which habit wastes water

quiz.q: A tap leaks 200 ml an hour. How much does it leak in 5 hours?
Two taps leak 6 L and 4 L each day. How much water is wasted in a day?
How many hours are there in a day, for working out daily water loss?
quiz.explain: A day has 24 hours.

quiz.q: Water from washing vegetables can be...
quiz.explain: Reusing water for plants saves fresh water.
quiz.mistake: Does not think of reusing water

teach.ask: Gappu's tap is dripping. Gappu says it is only a little water. How would you show how much is wasted?
teach.praise: One hour times 24 is a lot in a day, and even more in a week! I will get it fixed.
teach.nudge: How can you measure the leak, and how do you find the loss for a day?

learn.hook: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time on a number line: 3, 6, 9, 12... Will it ever land on 20?
points: Jumping in equal steps from 0 lands on multiples: jumps of 4 land on 4, 8, 12, 16, 20...
A number is reached by a jump if it is a multiple of the jump size: 20 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 5) but not of 3.
The number of jumps to reach a target is target ÷ jump size: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 jumps.
The smallest 3-digit number reached by jumps of 8 is 104 (8 × 13).
Bigger jumps reach a number in fewer jumps: to reach 24, a 3-jumper needs 8 jumps, an 8-jumper needs only 3.

example.q: A rabbit jumps 4 at a time from 0. How many jumps to reach 36?

learn.reallife: Skipping steps on a staircase two or three at a time, you land only on certain steps: the multiples!

quiz.q: A frog jumps 3 at a time from 0. Which number will it land on?
quiz.explain: 21 = 3 × 7, so it is a multiple of 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number close to a multiple

quiz.q: A deer jumps 6 at a time. How many jumps to reach 48?
quiz.explain: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 jumps.

quiz.q: A kangaroo jumps 8 at a time. Does it land on 60?
options: Yes, it lands on every number
No, 60 is not a multiple of 8
quiz.explain: 8 × 7 = 56 and 8 × 8 = 64. It jumps over 60.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every even number is a multiple of 8

quiz.q: What is the smallest 3-digit number a 4-jumper lands on?
quiz.explain: 100 = 4 × 25, and 100 is the smallest 3-digit number.

quiz.q: What is the smallest 3-digit number an 8-jumper lands on?
To reach 24, how many more jumps does a 3-jumper need than a 6-jumper?
Which number is a multiple of 4?
quiz.mistake: Thinks all even numbers are multiples of 4

quiz.q: A grasshopper jumps 6 at a time and lands on 54. How many jumps did it make?

teach.ask: Gappu jumps 4 at a time on a number line. Will Gappu land on 30? Explain how to check.
teach.praise: 28 and 32 are multiples of 4, but 30 is not. I jump right over it!
teach.nudge: Is 30 in the 4 times table?

learn.hook: A 3-jumper and a 4-jumper start together at 0. Where do they first land on the same number?
points: A common multiple is a number that is a multiple of both jump sizes.
The first common landing point of 3 and 4 is 12. For 6 and 8 it is 24.
In a chase, two jumpers meet where their multiples match.
In a multiplication chart, colour the rows of two numbers to see their common multiples.

example.q: A cat jumps 6 at a time and a rat jumps 4 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first meet?

learn.reallife: If one bell rings every 3 minutes and another every 4 minutes, they ring together every 12 minutes!

quiz.q: What is the first common landing point of a 3-jumper and a 4-jumper?
What is the first common landing point of a 6-jumper and an 8-jumper?
Which number is a common multiple of 2 and 5?
quiz.explain: 20 is in both tables: 2 × 10 and 5 × 4.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of only one number

quiz.q: A cat jumps 5 at a time and a rat 3 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first meet?
Which is NOT a common multiple of 3 and 4?
quiz.explain: 18 is a multiple of 3 but not of 4.

quiz.q: On a multiplication chart, you colour the 3s row and the 4s row. Which number is coloured in both?
quiz.explain: 12 = 3 × 4 = 4 × 3, so it is in both rows.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number from only one row

quiz.q: Two frogs jump 4 and 6 at a time from 0. Where do they meet for the SECOND time?
quiz.explain: Common multiples of 4 and 6: 12, 24, 36. The second is 24.

quiz.q: Common multiples of 2 and 3 between 1 and 20: how many are there?
quiz.explain: 6, 12 and 18. That is 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts multiples of only one number

teach.ask: Gappu and a friend jump 3 and 4 at a time. Gappu wants to know where they land together. Explain.
teach.praise: List both and look for the same number. 12 is our first meeting point!
teach.nudge: How can you find numbers that both jumpers land on?

learn.hook: 4 plates with 6 laddoos on each. Count one by one? No way! Multiply!
points: Multiplication is a quick way to add equal groups.
An array is objects in rows and columns. 3 rows of 7 = 3 × 7 = 21.
Order does not change the answer: 6 × 4 = 4 × 6.
Any number × 1 = the same number. Any number × 0 = 0.

example.q: A rangoli has 3 rows of diyas with 7 diyas in each row. How many diyas are there?

learn.reallife: Eggs in trays, chairs in rows and seats in a train coach are all equal groups.

quiz.q: There are 4 plates with 6 laddoos on each plate. How many laddoos are there?
quiz.explain: 4 groups of 6 is 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24. That is 4 × 6.

quiz.q: A rangoli has 3 rows of diyas with 7 diyas in each row. How many diyas are there?
quiz.explain: 3 rows of 7 is 3 × 7 = 21.
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and the diyas in a row

quiz.q: What is 8 × 7?
quiz.explain: 8 × 7 = 56. You can think 8 × 7 = 7 × 8.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?
quiz.explain: There are 6 fives, so it is 6 × 5 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Miscounts how many fives are added

quiz.q: What is 9 × 6?
Each auto-rickshaw carries 3 children to school. How many children do 9 autos carry?
quiz.explain: 9 groups of 3 = 9 × 3 = 27.

quiz.q: What is 0 × 845?
quiz.explain: Zero groups of anything is nothing. Any number × 0 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplying by 0 leaves the number the same

quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the answer. 6 × 4 = 4 × 6 = 24.
quiz.mistake: Writes the answer 24 instead of the missing number

teach.ask: Gappu has 5 baskets with 4 mangoes in each. Gappu is counting one by one. Is there a faster way?
teach.praise: Yes! 5 equal groups of 4 is 5 × 4 = 20. Multiplying is so fast!
teach.nudge: Are the baskets equal? What can Gappu do with equal groups?

learn.hook: Gulabo's flowers have 5 petals each. She counts 80 petals. How many flowers is that?
points: To find the number of groups, divide the total by the size of each group: 80 ÷ 5 = 16 flowers.
In 4 × 6 = 24, 4 is the multiplier (how many groups), 6 is the multiplicand (size of each group), 24 is the product.
Tray problems: total = number of trays × items per tray. Trays needed = total ÷ items per tray.
The same number can be arranged in different arrays: 24 = 1 × 24 = 2 × 12 = 3 × 8 = 4 × 6.

example.q: How many different arrays can you make with 12 laddoos (count 3 × 4 and 4 × 3 as different)?

learn.reallife: Chairs in a hall, eggs in a tray and seedlings in a nursery are all arranged in arrays.

quiz.q: Gulabo counts 80 petals. Each flower has 5 petals. How many flowers?
quiz.explain: 80 ÷ 5 = 16 flowers.

quiz.q: In 7 × 4 = 28, which number is the product?
quiz.explain: The product is the answer of a multiplication.

quiz.q: An array has 5 rows with 8 stars in each row. Which multiplication fits it?
quiz.explain: Rows × items in a row: 5 × 8 = 40.

quiz.q: A baker has 6 trays with 9 buns each. How many buns?
A shop has 56 cups. Each tray holds 8 cups. How many trays are needed?
quiz.explain: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 trays.

quiz.q: Which is NOT an array for 24?
How many plants are in each row if 36 plants are planted in 4 equal rows?
In '3 × 6 = 18 (3 groups of 6)', what is 6 called?
quiz.explain: 6 is the size of each group, the multiplicand. 3 is the multiplier.

teach.ask: Gappu has 24 seedlings and wants to plant them in neat rows. Show Gappu some ways.
teach.praise: 4 rows of 6 or 3 rows of 8, both make 24! So many ways.
teach.nudge: Which pairs of numbers multiply to 24?

learn.hook: Double 37? Double the 30, double the 7, add. 60 + 14 = 74. Magic!
points: Doubling means multiplying by 2: double 9 = 18.
Double a 2-digit number by doubling the tens and the ones: double 37 = 60 + 14 = 74.
The ones digit of a double depends only on the ones digit: double of a number ending in 7 ends in 4 (7 + 7 = 14).
Any doubled number is even, because it is made of two equal halves.

example.q: Double 48.

learn.reallife: Recipes for twice as many guests need double the ingredients: double 250 g sugar is 500 g!

quiz.q: What is double 36?
Double 45 = ?
Without doubling fully, what is the ones digit of double 58?
quiz.explain: 8 + 8 = 16, so the ones digit is 6. (Double 58 = 116.)

quiz.q: Is double any number even or odd?
quiz.explain: A double is two equal groups, so it can always be paired: even.
quiz.mistake: Thinks double an odd number is odd

quiz.q: Double 27 = ?
Which number can NOT be a doubled whole number?
quiz.explain: 51 is odd. Doubles are always even.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the even rule

quiz.q: Double a number ending in 4 ends in which digit?
Mamta doubles her savings of ₹125. How much does she have now?
quiz.mistake: Doubles only part of the number

teach.ask: Gappu needs to double 47 quickly. Teach Gappu the tens-and-ones trick.
teach.praise: Double 40 is 80, double 7 is 14, together 94! Doubling magic!
teach.nudge: What do you get when you double the tens and the ones separately?

learn.hook: A multiplication chart is full of hidden patterns. Fold it along the diagonal and the two halves match!
points: In a multiplication chart, each box = row number × column number.
Order does not change the product: 3 × 4 = 4 × 3 = 12. So the chart is the same on both sides of the diagonal.
The diagonal from the top-left shows square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36...
Rows of even numbers (2, 4, 6...) have only even products.
Rows of odd numbers (3, 5, 7...) go odd, even, odd, even.

example.q: Which box of the chart has row 6 and column 7? What else has the same number?

learn.reallife: Multiplication charts hang in many classrooms. Spotting patterns makes the tables easier to remember!

games.title: Chart patterns
items: Order does not change the product.
Every number in the 6s row is even.
6 is even, so all its products are even.
The 3s row is all odd numbers.
It goes 3, 6, 9, 12... odd, even, odd, even.

items.text: Row 7, column 8 = ___
Row 9, column 9 = ___
Row 5, column 6 = ___
The 4th square number on the diagonal is ___

quiz.q: What number is in row 8, column 6 of a multiplication chart?
Row 4, column 7 shows 28. Which other box also shows 28 because order does not matter?
quiz.mistake: Does not use the order rule

quiz.q: Which numbers are on the diagonal of the chart?
quiz.explain: The diagonal has 1 × 1, 2 × 2, 3 × 3... the square numbers.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the diagonal with a row

quiz.q: What is the 6th square number (6 × 6)?
Which row of the chart has ONLY even numbers?
quiz.explain: 8 is even, so every product in its row is even.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd rows can be all even

quiz.q: In the 5s row: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. What pattern do you see?
quiz.explain: 5 is odd, so its row alternates odd and even.

quiz.q: Is 7 × 9 the same as 9 × 7?
quiz.explain: Order does not change the product.

quiz.q: Folding the chart along the diagonal, the box 3 × 8 lands on which box?
quiz.explain: The halves match because 3 × 8 = 8 × 3.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the mirror pattern

teach.ask: Gappu learnt 6 × 8 but forgot 8 × 6. Explain why Gappu already knows it, using the chart.
teach.praise: 6 × 8 and 8 × 6 are both 48! The chart is the same on both sides of the diagonal.
teach.nudge: Does changing the order change the product?

learn.hook: The 8 times table ends in 8, 6, 4, 2, 0, then 8, 6, 4, 2, 0 again. Can you guess the ones digit of 12 × 8?
points: In each row, the ones digits repeat in a cycle. Row of 8: 8, 6, 4, 2, 0, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0.
Use the cycle to predict beyond the chart: 11 × 8 ends in 8 and 12 × 8 ends in 6 (88 and 96).
Some digits never appear: in the 8s row, no product ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.
In the 5s row, products end only in 5 or 0.
A product ends in 0 when one number is a multiple of 10, or when a number ending in 5 is multiplied by an even number.

example.q: What is the ones digit of 13 × 8?

learn.reallife: Cashiers often check bills by looking at the last digit. If 5 items cost ₹8 each, the total must end in 0!

quiz.q: What is the ones digit of 11 × 8?
quiz.explain: 11 × 8 = 88. The cycle 8, 6, 4, 2, 0 starts again at 11.

quiz.q: What is 12 × 8, and does its ones digit fit the cycle?
quiz.explain: 12 × 8 = 96. The ones digit 6 is next after 8 in the cycle.

quiz.q: Which digit NEVER appears as the ones digit in the 8s table?
quiz.explain: All products of 8 are even, so they never end in 5 (or any odd digit).
quiz.mistake: Picks a digit from the cycle

quiz.q: In the 5s table, which ones digits appear?
Which product ends in 0?
quiz.explain: 5 × 8 = 40. Five times an even number ends in 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any product with 5 ends in 5

quiz.q: What is the ones digit of 15 × 8?
quiz.explain: 15 × 8 = 120. In the cycle, every 5th product ends in 0.

quiz.q: How many different ones digits appear in the 2s table?
quiz.explain: 2, 4, 6, 8, 0: five digits.

quiz.q: Which multiplication gives a product ending in 0?
quiz.explain: 6 × 15 = 90. 15 has a 5, and 6 is even.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the ones digit of 14 × 8 without the full sum. Show Gappu the cycle trick.
teach.praise: 8, 6, 4, 2, 0 again and again: 14 × 8 ends in 2! (It is 112.)
teach.nudge: What pattern do the ones digits of the 8s table make?

learn.hook: 40 × 6? Think 4 tens × 6 = 24 tens = 240. Multiplying by tens is easy!
points: Multiply multiples of 10 using basic facts: 40 × 6 = 4 tens × 6 = 24 tens = 240.
Wheels on many vehicles: 30 cycles have 30 × 2 = 60 wheels; 20 cars have 20 × 4 = 80 wheels.
Multi-step problems: find each part, then add. 12 geese (2 legs) and 15 sheep (4 legs): 24 + 60 = 84 legs.
Make up your own story for an expression like 16 × 5: 'Each box has 16 crayons. How many crayons in 5 boxes?'

example.q: In a farm there are 14 hens and 9 goats. How many legs in all?

learn.reallife: Parking lots, bus depots and cycle stands: counting wheels is real maths for the people who run them!

quiz.q: What is 40 × 6?
What is 70 × 8?
A cycle stand has 30 cycles. How many wheels?
A parking lot has 20 cars and 10 auto-rickshaws (3 wheels each). How many wheels in all?
A farm has 12 geese and 15 sheep. How many legs in all?
A hall has 18 rows of 6 seats. 25 seats are empty. How many are filled?
Which story fits 14 × 5?
quiz.explain: 5 groups of 14 is 14 × 5.
quiz.mistake: Picks an addition or division story

quiz.q: Books are in 7 piles of 23. How many books?

teach.ask: Gappu has to find 60 × 7. Explain the quick way.
teach.nudge: Which basic fact helps, and what does the zero do?

learn.hook: A bus has 48 seats. How many seats in 4 buses? Let's multiply big numbers!
points: Break the bigger number into tens and ones: 23 = 20 + 3.
Multiply each part and add: 23 × 3 = 20 × 3 + 3 × 3 = 60 + 9 = 69.
In column method, multiply the ones first. If you get 10 or more, carry to the tens.
To multiply by 10, put a 0 at the end: 34 × 10 = 340.

example.q: Find 17 × 6.

learn.reallife: A school counts how many students fit in 4 buses, or how many diyas are needed for 8 rows of 15.

quiz.q: What is 23 × 3?
What is 45 × 2?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply the ones part

quiz.q: What is 34 × 10?
quiz.explain: Multiplying by 10 puts a 0 at the end. 34 × 10 = 340.

quiz.q: What is 17 × 6?
A school bus has 48 seats. How many seats are there in 4 such buses?
What is 25 × 4?
What is 125 × 3?
For Diwali, Kabir makes 8 rows of diyas with 15 diyas in each row. How many diyas is that?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find 24 × 3 but only knows small tables. How can Gappu do it?
teach.praise: Brilliant! 20 × 3 = 60 and 4 × 3 = 12, so 60 + 12 = 72. Gappu can multiply big numbers now!
teach.nudge: Can Gappu break 24 into smaller, easier parts first?

learn.hook: 20 laddoos, 4 friends. How many each so nobody fights? Division shares fairly!
points: Division means sharing equally or making equal groups.
20 ÷ 4 = 5 means 20 shared among 4 gives 5 each.
Division is the opposite of multiplication. If 6 × 9 = 54, then 54 ÷ 9 = 6 and 54 ÷ 6 = 9.
Sometimes things are left over. This is the remainder. 17 shared among 5 gives 3 each and 2 left over.

example.q: 48 pencils are packed in boxes of 6. How many boxes are needed?

learn.reallife: Sharing sweets, putting children into teams and packing things in boxes all use division.

quiz.q: 20 laddoos are shared equally among 4 friends. How many does each friend get?
What is 18 ÷ 3?
35 marbles are put in groups of 7. How many groups are there?
quiz.mistake: Gives the size of each group instead of the number of groups

quiz.q: What is 56 ÷ 8?
If 6 × 9 = 54, what is 54 ÷ 9?
quiz.explain: Division undoes multiplication. 6 × 9 = 54, so 54 ÷ 9 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how multiplication and division are linked

quiz.q: 17 bananas are shared equally among 5 monkeys. How many bananas are left over?
quiz.explain: Each monkey gets 3 bananas (5 × 3 = 15). 17 - 15 = 2 are left over.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number each monkey gets (3) instead of the remainder

quiz.q: 48 pencils are packed in boxes of 6. How many boxes are needed?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 6 from 48 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Kabir reads 63 pages of a story book in 7 days. He reads the same number of pages each day. How many pages does he read daily?

teach.ask: Gappu has 12 berries and 3 friends. How can Gappu share them fairly?
teach.praise: Thank you! 12 ÷ 3 = 4 each, because 3 × 4 = 12. Everyone is happy!
teach.nudge: How many berries should each friend get so it is fair? Which times table helps?

topics.title: Division: repeated subtraction and place value

learn.hook: 96 sweets in boxes of 8? Take away 10 boxes (80) and then 2 boxes (16). That's 12 boxes!
points: Divide by taking away groups: from 96, take 10 groups of 8 (80), leaving 16; then 2 groups of 8 (16). Total 12 groups.
With a place-value table: 88 ÷ 4 → 8 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens; 8 ones ÷ 4 = 2 ones. So 22.
Write division stories: '72 pencils are shared among 6 friends. How many each?' 72 ÷ 6 = 12.
A multiplication like 6 × 7 = 42 hides two divisions: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 and 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Look for such number families in a grid.

example.q: Divide 84 by 7 using repeated subtraction of groups.

learn.reallife: When packing mangoes in crates, a farmer fills 10 crates at a time, then the rest. That is division by repeated subtraction!

quiz.q: What is 88 ÷ 4 using tens and ones?
quiz.explain: 8 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens; 8 ones ÷ 4 = 2 ones. So 22.

quiz.q: 96 ÷ 8: Riya takes away 10 groups of 8 first. How much is left?
Riya then takes 2 more groups of 8 from 16. What is 96 ÷ 8?
quiz.explain: 10 groups + 2 groups = 12.

quiz.q: What is 69 ÷ 3?
quiz.explain: 6 tens ÷ 3 = 2 tens; 9 ones ÷ 3 = 3. So 23.

quiz.q: Which story fits 72 ÷ 6?
quiz.explain: Sharing 72 among 6 is division.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiplication or addition story

quiz.q: If 8 × 9 = 72, which division is true?
quiz.explain: Multiplication and division are partners: 72 ÷ 9 = 8.

quiz.q: A grid shows the numbers 7, 6, 42 in a row. Which sentence can be shaded?
quiz.explain: 7 × 6 = 42 is a true multiplication sentence.

quiz.q: A teacher has 84 stickers for 7 children. How many does each get?

teach.ask: Gappu has 96 marbles to put in bags of 8. Gappu does not know the 12 times table. Show another way.
teach.praise: Take away 10 bags of 8 (80), then 2 more (16). 12 bags!
teach.nudge: Can you take away big groups of 8 first?

points: Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end: 7 × 100 = 700.
Patterns: 6 × 5 = 30, 6 × 50 = 300, 6 × 500 = 3000. One more zero each time.
Split a 3-digit number into hundreds, tens and ones to multiply: 125 × 8 = 100 × 8 + 20 × 8 + 5 × 8.
Write a story for 245 × 4: 'A school collects ₹245 from each of 4 classes. How much in all?'

example.q: A box has 136 pencils. How many pencils in 4 boxes?

learn.reallife: When a school orders notebooks for many classes, the bill uses 3-digit × 1-digit multiplication.

quiz.q: What is 9 × 100?
quiz.explain: Multiplying by 100 adds two zeros: 900.

quiz.q: What is 4 × 300?
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 = 12, so 4 × 3 hundreds = 12 hundreds = 1200.
Each time the 5 gets a zero, the product gets a zero: 3000.

quiz.q: What is 125 × 8?
A box has 145 pencils. How many pencils in 6 boxes?
Each of 7 classes collects ₹235 for a trip. How much in all?
quiz.mistake: Makes an error in one part

quiz.q: Which story fits 312 × 3?
options: 3 buses each carry 312 bags of rice
quiz.explain: 3 groups of 312 is 312 × 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a story that is not multiplication

quiz.q: What is 3 × 800?
quiz.explain: 3 × 8 = 24, so 24 hundreds = 2400.

teach.ask: Gappu must find 213 × 4. Show Gappu how splitting into hundreds, tens and ones helps.
teach.praise: 800 + 40 + 12 = 852! Splitting makes it easy.
teach.nudge: How do you split 213, and what do you do with each part?

topics.title: More division and patterns in division

learn.hook: 108 people want to cross a river in 9 boats, with the same number in each boat. How many per boat?
points: Divide a bigger number by splitting it: 108 ÷ 9 → 90 ÷ 9 = 10 and 18 ÷ 9 = 2. So 12.
Divide multiples of 10 and 100 using basic facts: 600 ÷ 6 = 100; 800 ÷ 4 = 200.
Word problems: 240 children, 40 per bus → 240 ÷ 40 = 6 buses.
If there is a remainder, decide if you need one more group: 50 people, 6 per raft → 8 rafts take 48, so 9 rafts are needed for everyone.

example.q: 50 people need to cross a river. Each raft takes 6 people. How many rafts are needed?
steps: 2 people are left, so 1 more raft is needed.

learn.reallife: School trips need enough buses for every child, so we always round up when people are left over!

games.title: Remainders and extra groups
items: 50 people, 6 per raft: 9 rafts are needed.
8 rafts carry 48; 2 more need a 9th raft.
25 laddoos in boxes of 4: 6 full boxes and 1 left over.
43 children, 10 per car: 4 cars carry everyone.
4 cars carry 40; 3 more need a 5th car.

quiz.q: 108 people go in 9 boats equally. How many in each boat?

quiz.explain: 9 hundreds ÷ 3 = 3 hundreds = 300.

quiz.q: What is 800 ÷ 4?
quiz.explain: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so 8 hundreds ÷ 4 = 2 hundreds = 200.

quiz.q: 240 children go on a trip. Each bus takes 40. How many buses?
quiz.explain: 24 tens ÷ 4 tens = 6.

quiz.q: 45 people, 8 per raft. How many rafts are needed so everyone crosses?
quiz.explain: 45 ÷ 8 = 5 remainder 5. 5 rafts carry 40, and 5 people need a 6th raft.

quiz.q: A shopkeeper packs 38 eggs in trays of 6. How many FULL trays?
quiz.explain: 6 × 6 = 36. 6 full trays, 2 eggs left.
quiz.mistake: Counts the leftover as a full tray

quiz.q: What is 600 ÷ 3?
A bus seats 50. How many buses for 320 people?
quiz.explain: 320 ÷ 50 = 6 remainder 20. 6 buses carry 300; 20 more need a 7th bus.

teach.ask: 43 children need to go to the zoo in cars of 10. Gappu says 4 cars. Is Gappu right?
teach.praise: 4 cars carry 40, and 3 children would be left behind. We need 5 cars!
teach.nudge: What happens to the children left over?

learn.hook: Tara saves ₹45 a week for 8 weeks and shares it equally with 3 friends... wait, is that 4 people? Read carefully!
points: Multi-step problems may need both × and ÷: first find a total, then share it.
Some questions cannot be answered from the given facts. Check what is told and what is asked.
Practise multiplying and dividing 2- and 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers, with remainders.
Some statements are always true (any number × 1 = itself), some sometimes true, and some never true.

example.q: Tara saves ₹45 a week for 8 weeks. She shares the money equally with her 3 friends (4 people in all). How much does each get?

learn.reallife: Planning a picnic with friends means multiplying costs and then dividing them fairly.

games.title: Always, sometimes or never true?
items: The product is bigger than both numbers

quiz.q: Ravi saves ₹35 a week for 6 weeks, then shares it equally among 3 people. How much does each get?
'A shop sold 24 pens on Monday.' Which question can be answered from this?
options: How many pens were sold on Monday?
How much did the pens cost?
quiz.explain: Only the number sold on Monday is given.
quiz.mistake: Picks a question that needs more information

quiz.q: What is 57 ÷ 5?
What is 216 × 3?
'The product of two numbers is always bigger than both numbers.' Is this always, sometimes or never true?
quiz.explain: True for 3 × 4 = 12, but false for 5 × 1 = 5 or 7 × 0 = 0.

quiz.q: 'Any number multiplied by 1 is the same number.' Is this always, sometimes or never true?
quiz.explain: 1 group of a number is just that number.

quiz.q: A class collects ₹128 from each of 5 groups. The money is shared equally by 4 teams for a project. How much does each team get?
'A box holds 12 apples.' What else do you need to know to find the total apples?
quiz.explain: Total = apples per box × number of boxes, so you need the number of boxes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the question can be answered already

teach.ask: Gappu says multiplying always makes a number bigger. Is Gappu always right? Explain with examples.
teach.praise: 5 × 1 = 5 and 5 × 0 = 0! So it is only sometimes true.
teach.nudge: What happens when you multiply by 1 or by 0?

topics.title: Race to the target: a winning strategy

learn.hook: Two players start at 0 and take turns adding 1 or 2. Whoever says 10 wins. Is there a way to always win?
points: Rules: start at 0. On your turn, add 1 or 2 to the total. The player who reaches the target wins.
Work backward: if you say 7, your partner can only reach 8 or 9, and you then reach 10.
So for target 10 the winning numbers are 10, 7, 4, 1. Each is 3 less than the one after it.
If you start, say 1 first and keep landing on 4, 7 and 10.
Change the target and the winning numbers change: for 11 they are 2, 5, 8, 11; for 12 they are 3, 6, 9, 12.

example.q: Target 11. Which numbers should you try to say?

learn.reallife: Strategy games like this train you to think ahead, like a chess player planning moves.

games.title: Race facts
items: For target 10, saying 7 makes you win.
Your partner reaches 8 or 9, then you reach 10.
For target 12, the first player can say 3 on the first turn.
On the first turn you can only say 1 or 2.
Adding 1 or 2 means your partner and you together add 3.
For target 11, you should say 2 first.
It does not matter what you say; it is all luck.

quiz.q: Target 10. Your partner says 8. What should you say to win?
quiz.explain: 8 + 2 = 10, so add 2 and say 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 and gives the win away

quiz.q: Target 10. Which number should you say to be sure of winning on your next turn?
quiz.explain: After 7, your partner says 8 or 9, and you can reach 10.

quiz.q: Target 10. What are all the winning numbers?
quiz.explain: Count back in 3s from 10: 7, 4, 1.

quiz.q: Target 11. What should the first player say?
quiz.explain: Winning numbers for 11 are 11, 8, 5, 2. Say 2 first.

quiz.q: Target 12. Winning numbers are 3, 6, 9, 12. Who can win if both play well?
quiz.explain: The first player can only say 1 or 2, so the second player can always reach 3.

quiz.q: Target 15. Which is a winning number?
Why do winning numbers go up by 3?
options: Your partner adds 1 or 2 and you add the rest to make 3
quiz.explain: If your partner adds 1, you add 2; if they add 2, you add 1. Together it is always 3.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how the two moves combine

quiz.q: Target 20. Starting at 0, what should the first player say?
quiz.explain: Count back in 3s from 20: 17, 14, 11, 8, 5, 2. Say 2.

teach.ask: Gappu keeps losing the race-to-10 game. Teach Gappu the winning trick.
teach.praise: Say 1, 4, 7 and then 10! Counting back in 3s from the target wins every time.
teach.nudge: Which number should you say just before your partner's last turn?

learn.hook: Make a chart where each box is row number + column number. Then hunt for patterns!
points: In an addition chart (rows and columns 1 to 10), each box = row number + column number.
Moving right along a row, numbers go up by 1. Moving down a column, they go up by 1.
Moving diagonally down to the right, numbers go up by 2. Along the other diagonal they stay the same.
A sum appears as many times as there are ways to make it: 5 = 1 + 4 = 2 + 3 = 3 + 2 = 4 + 1, so 5 appears 4 times.
11 appears the most (10 times) in a 1 to 10 chart.

example.q: In a 1 to 10 addition chart, how many times does 4 appear?

learn.reallife: Hundred charts and addition charts in your classroom are full of patterns that make adding faster.

items.text: Row 6, column 7 = ___
Row 9, column 9 = ___
Moving right one box adds ___.
Moving diagonally down-right adds ___.

games.title: How many times in a 1 to 10 chart?

quiz.q: In an addition chart, what is in row 7, column 5?
Moving one box to the right in an addition chart, the number...
quiz.explain: The column number goes up by 1, so the sum goes up by 1.

quiz.q: Moving diagonally down and to the right, the number goes up by how much?
quiz.explain: Both the row and column go up by 1: 1 + 1 = 2.

quiz.q: Along the diagonal going down to the LEFT, what happens to the numbers?
quiz.explain: The row goes up by 1 and the column down by 1, so the sum stays the same.

quiz.q: In a 1 to 10 addition chart, how many times does the sum 6 appear?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 2 + 4 and 4 + 2 are different boxes

quiz.q: Which sum appears the most in a 1 to 10 addition chart?
How many times does 20 appear in a 1 to 10 chart?
Why does 3 appear twice in the chart?
quiz.explain: Each way of making 3 is a different box: row 1 column 2, and row 2 column 1.
quiz.mistake: Does not link boxes to ways of adding

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know why 11 appears so many times in the addition chart. Explain.
teach.praise: There are 10 ways to make 11, so it fills 10 boxes!
teach.nudge: How many pairs of numbers from 1 to 10 add to 11?

topics.title: Odd and even sums, window frames and a grid puzzle

learn.hook: Odd + odd = even. Even + even = even. Odd + even = odd. Always! Can you use this to solve a puzzle?
points: Odd + odd = even (3 + 5 = 8). Even + even = even (4 + 6 = 10). Odd + even = odd (3 + 4 = 7).
Differences work the same way: odd − even and even − odd are odd; odd − odd and even − even are even.
Window frame: in any 2 by 2 square of the addition chart, the two diagonal sums are equal.
This works for the corners of a 3 by 3 frame too.
Puzzle: place 1 to 9 in a 3 by 3 grid so neighbours always differ by an odd number. Put odd numbers in the corners and centre, even numbers in the edge boxes.

example.q: In the addition chart, a 2 by 2 window has 7, 8 on top and 8, 9 below. Check the diagonal sums.

learn.reallife: Knowing odd and even rules lets you check sums quickly: 347 + 528 must be odd, because odd + even = odd!

games.title: Window frames and the puzzle
items: In a 2 by 2 window of the addition chart, diagonal sums are equal.
Both diagonals add to the same number.
In the grid puzzle, putting an odd next to an even gives an odd difference.
Two odd numbers next to each other give an odd difference.
The 3 by 3 puzzle uses 5 odd numbers and 4 even numbers.
In a 3 by 3 window of the chart, the corner diagonal sums are different.

quiz.q: What kind of number is odd + odd?
quiz.explain: Two odd numbers each have one left over; the two leftovers pair up. So the sum is even.

quiz.q: Without adding, is 347 + 528 odd or even?
quiz.explain: 347 is odd and 528 is even. Odd + even = odd.

quiz.q: Which sum is even?
quiz.explain: 23 and 45 are both odd. Odd + odd = even (68).
quiz.mistake: Thinks one odd number makes it odd

quiz.q: A 2 by 2 window in the addition chart shows 5, 6 on top and 6, 7 below. What are the diagonal sums?
A 3 by 3 frame in the addition chart has corners 4 and 6 on top, 6 and 8 at the bottom. What is the sum of each diagonal of corners?
In the 3 by 3 grid puzzle, neighbours must differ by an odd number. What must the neighbours of an odd number be?
quiz.explain: Odd − even is odd, but odd − odd is even. So an odd number needs even neighbours.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd neighbours give odd differences

quiz.q: In the puzzle, the centre box touches 4 boxes. If an odd number goes in the centre, what goes in those 4 boxes?
quiz.explain: The centre's 4 neighbours must be even: 2, 4, 6, 8.
quiz.mistake: Places odd numbers next to the odd centre

quiz.q: What is 6 + 8 + 3? Is it odd or even?
quiz.explain: 6 + 8 = 14 (even). 14 + 3 = 17 (even + odd = odd).

teach.ask: Gappu must place 1 to 9 in a 3 by 3 grid so neighbours always differ by an odd number. How should Gappu plan it?
teach.praise: Odd numbers in the corners and centre, even numbers on the edges. Every neighbour pair is odd and even!
teach.nudge: What kind of difference do an odd and an even number make?

learn.hook: Take 27. Reverse it: 72. Add: 99. Try 34 + 43 = 77. Notice anything?
points: Reverse a 2-digit number by swapping its digits: 27 → 72.
A number plus its reverse is always a multiple of 11: 27 + 72 = 99 = 9 × 11.
The sum is 11 × (sum of the digits): for 27, 2 + 7 = 9, and 11 × 9 = 99.
Numbers whose reverse-sum is 55 have digits adding to 5: 14, 23, 32, 41.
The smallest 3-digit reverse-sum is 110 (digits adding to 10, like 19 + 91).

example.q: Find 46 + its reverse. Check with the digit-sum rule.

learn.reallife: Number tricks like this are fun to show your family. Ask them to pick a number and you predict the sum!

quiz.q: What is 27 + 72?
A number plus its reverse is always a multiple of which number?
quiz.explain: ab + ba = 11 × (a + b).
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is a multiple of 10

quiz.q: Which number gives a reverse-sum of 55?
quiz.explain: 23 + 32 = 55. Its digits add to 5.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number with a 5 in it

quiz.q: Which number gives a reverse-sum of 88?
quiz.explain: 44 + 44 = 88. Its digits add to 8. (34 gives 77, 45 gives 99, 48 gives 132.)
quiz.mistake: Does not use the digit-sum rule

quiz.q: How many 2-digit numbers (with no zero digit) have a reverse-sum of 55?
quiz.explain: Digits adding to 5 with no zero: 14, 23, 32, 41. That is 4.

quiz.q: What is the smallest 3-digit number you can get as a reverse-sum?
quiz.explain: The sum is 11 × (digit sum). 11 × 9 = 99 is 2-digit; 11 × 10 = 110.

quiz.q: Use the rule: what is 38 + 83?
Rani's reverse-sum is 132. What do her digits add to?
quiz.explain: 132 = 11 × 12, so the digits add to 12 (like 57 + 75).

teach.ask: Gappu tried 25 + 52 and 36 + 63 and got 77 and 99. Gappu wonders what the secret is. Explain.
teach.praise: Every reverse-sum is 11 times the digit sum! 2 + 5 = 7, 11 × 7 = 77.
teach.nudge: Which number divides every reverse-sum, and how is it linked to the digits?

learn.hook: 1,250, 1,275, 1,300, ... What comes next? Count in 25s!
points: To continue a sequence, find the step: the difference between two neighbours.
Sequences can go up or down in equal steps of 25, 50, 100 or 1,000.
On a number line with big jumps, mark each jump: 2,000, 3,000, 4,000...
To find a missing number in the middle, add the step to the number before it.
learn.reallife: Odometers, page numbers in thick books and counting money in ₹50 notes all use big skip counts.

quiz.explain: It goes down by 1,000 each time.

quiz.q: On a number line, jumps of 1,000 start at 2,500. Where is the 3rd jump?

quiz.mistake: Looks only at the last digits

quiz.q: Count by 50 from 4,850. What are the next two numbers?
A number line has marks at 1,000, 2,000, 3,000. Where is 2,500?
quiz.explain: 2,500 is 500 more than 2,000, halfway to 3,000.

teach.ask: Gappu sees 7,250, 7,300, 7,350 and wants the next number. How can Gappu find it?
teach.praise: The step is 50, so the next is 7,400!
teach.nudge: How much does the sequence go up by each time?

topics.title: How many animals? Reading and changing counts

learn.hook: Forest officers count elephants, tigers and leopards. Let's read their numbers like wildlife detectives!
points: Read a data table carefully: find the animal (row) and the state (column).
'More than' means add: 250 more than 1,783 is 1,783 + 250 = 2,033.
To find an earlier count, subtract the change: if there are 3,128 now after an increase of 215, earlier there were 3,128 − 215 = 2,913.
We can show animal counts on a map by writing each number on its state.

example.q: Now there are 785 tigers in a reserve after 128 were added since the last count. How many were there before?

learn.reallife: India counts its tigers every few years. Comparing counts tells us if conservation is working.

quiz.q: Practice table (made-up numbers), State A / State B: elephants 6,049 / 3,128; tigers 524 / 785; leopards 1,783 / 1,690. How many elephants are in State B?
quiz.explain: Find the elephant row and State B: 3,128.
quiz.mistake: Reads the wrong row or column

quiz.q: Practice table (made-up numbers), State A / State B: elephants 6,049 / 3,128; tigers 524 / 785; leopards 1,783 / 1,690. How many tigers are there in both states together?
A park had 1,690 leopards. Now there are 250 more than that. How many now?
A state now has 3,128 elephants, which is 215 more than the last count. What was the last count?
quiz.explain: Earlier = now − increase = 3,128 − 215 = 2,913.
quiz.mistake: Adds the change instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Practice table (made-up numbers), State A / State B: elephants 6,049 / 3,128; tigers 524 / 785; leopards 1,783 / 1,690. How many more leopards are in State A than in State B?
On a map, you write 524 on State A for tigers. If State A gets 76 more tigers, what number should the map show?
A reserve has 1,200 deer now. Last year it had 135 fewer. How many deer last year?
Practice table (made-up numbers), State A / State B: elephants 6,049 / 3,128; tigers 524 / 785; leopards 1,783 / 1,690. Which animal has the biggest total in both states?
quiz.explain: Elephants: 6,049 + 3,128 = 9,177. Leopards: 3,473. Tigers: 1,309.

teach.ask: Gappu reads 'there are now 200 more tigers than last time, 785 in all'. Gappu wants the old number. Explain.
teach.praise: 785 − 200 = 585 tigers before. Subtract to go back in time!
teach.nudge: To find the earlier count, do you add or subtract the change?

learn.hook: Forest rangers count animals, trees and visitors. Their numbers get really big! Let's solve their problems.
points: Read the problem slowly. Write down the numbers you are given.
Decide what is asked: a total (add) or a difference (subtract)?
Line up the places carefully when you add or subtract 4-digit numbers.
Estimate first to check that your answer makes sense.

example.q: A wildlife park counted 1342 deer last year and 1518 deer this year. How many more deer are there this year?

learn.reallife: Forest departments count tigers, elephants and birds to know if the animals are safe and growing in number.

games.title: Add or subtract?
items: Visitors in the morning and evening altogether
How many more deer this year
Birds in two lakes in all
How many fewer leopards than tigers

quiz.q: A wildlife park counted 1342 deer last year and 1518 deer this year. How many more deer are there this year?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' means subtract. 1518 - 1342 = 176.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger in every place

quiz.q: One lake has 2465 birds and another has 3178 birds. How many birds are there in both lakes?
Visitors to a tiger reserve in 4 months were 4508, 4580, 4085 and 4805. Which is the largest?
quiz.explain: All have 4 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 5, 5, 0, 8. 4805 has 8 hundreds, the most.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit instead of the hundreds

quiz.q: A forest has 3456 trees. What is the place value of 4 in 3456?
quiz.explain: The 4 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 4 × 100 = 400.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit itself instead of its place value

quiz.q: A zoo had 2750 visitors in the morning and 1875 in the evening. How many visitors came that day?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry into the thousands

quiz.q: A safari park had 3980 visitors in a week. Which is the best estimate?
quiz.explain: 3980 is only 20 less than 4000, so about 4000 is the best estimate.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the thousands digit and says about 3000

quiz.q: Three elephant herds have 18, 27 and 15 elephants. How many elephants are there in all?
A tiger reserve wants to plant 5000 saplings. 3275 have been planted. How many are still left to plant?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that borrowing makes the thousands 1 less (gets 2725)

teach.ask: A ranger counted 2465 birds at one lake and 3178 at another. Gappu wants the total. How should Gappu do it?
teach.praise: Great! Line up the places, add from the ones and carry. 5643 birds! Gappu is a ranger now!
teach.nudge: Does 'total' mean add or subtract? Where should Gappu start adding?

topics.title: Data word problems: parks, juice and vehicles

learn.hook: A juice factory made 2,450 bottles on Monday and 375 more on Tuesday. How many on Tuesday? Let's solve real data puzzles!
points: Visitor problems: find the difference between two parks, or a missing value from a total.
'More than' means add; 'less than' means subtract: 375 more than 2,450 is 2,825.
Find each count from the relationships, then compare them.
Put counts in order from biggest to smallest to compare them easily.

example.q: Mango juice: 2,450 bottles. Orange juice: 375 more than mango. Apple juice: 600 less than orange. Order them from most to least.

learn.reallife: Factories, transport offices and national parks keep records like these and use them to plan.

quiz.q: Park A had 5,320 visitors and Park B had 4,875. How many more visited Park A?
Two parks had 8,000 visitors in all. One park had 4,650. How many visited the other?
A factory made 2,450 bottles of mango juice and 375 more bottles of orange juice. How many orange juice bottles?
Apple juice was 600 bottles less than 2,825. How many apple juice bottles?
Cars: 3,180. Bikes: 1,340 more than cars. How many bikes?
Autos: 1,235 less than 3,180 cars. How many autos?
Bikes 4,520, cars 3,180, autos 1,945. Which order is from least to most?
A park had 3,450 visitors on Saturday. On Sunday it had 1,275 more. How many visitors in both days?

teach.ask: Gappu reads 'orange juice is 375 more than mango juice (2,450)'. Gappu is not sure whether to add or subtract. Help.
teach.praise: 'More than' means add! 2,450 + 375 = 2,825.
teach.nudge: Does 'more than' tell you to add or subtract?

topics.title: Money: notes, coins and a bank deposit slip

learn.hook: Papa sends you to the bank with a bundle of notes. You must fill the deposit slip yourself!
points: Count each kind of note: number of notes × value. 3 notes of ₹500 = ₹1,500.
Add all the amounts in columns to get the total: line up thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
On a deposit slip, write the total in figures and in words: ₹2,900 = 'Two thousand nine hundred rupees only'.
Check the total by adding again in a different order.

example.q: Notes: 3 × ₹500, 4 × ₹200, 5 × ₹100, 2 × ₹50. What is the total? Write it in words.
steps: Two thousand nine hundred rupees only.

learn.reallife: Banks ask you to write amounts in words so nobody can change the figures on the slip.

items.text: ₹2,900 in words: Two thousand ___ hundred
₹4,050 in words: Four thousand ___

quiz.q: How much are 4 notes of ₹500 and 3 notes of ₹200?
Which is ₹3,405 in words?
options: Three thousand four hundred fifty rupees
Three thousand four hundred five rupees
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tens and ones

quiz.q: Notes: 2 × ₹500, 5 × ₹100, 3 × ₹10. What is the total?
Meera deposits ₹1,850 and later ₹2,375. How much did she deposit in all?
Why must the amount be written in words on a deposit slip?
options: So nobody can change the figures
quiz.explain: Words are hard to change, so they keep the amount safe.

quiz.q: A slip shows 6 notes of ₹200 and 8 coins of ₹10. What is the total?
quiz.mistake: Counts the number of notes and coins

teach.ask: Gappu must fill a bank slip for 2 notes of ₹500 and 3 notes of ₹100. How should Gappu do it?
teach.praise: ₹1,000 + ₹300 = ₹1,300, and I write 'One thousand three hundred rupees only'!
teach.nudge: How much is each kind of note worth, and how do you write the total in words?

topics.title: Quick ways and reasoning with big numbers

learn.hook: 5,010 + 95 in your head? Add 100, then take away 5. 5,105!
points: Round to a nearby number, then adjust: 5,010 + 95 = 5,010 + 100 − 5 = 5,105.
Compare expressions without fully calculating: 3,456 + 1,000 > 3,456 + 999, because 1,000 > 999.
Check subtraction with addition: if 6,000 − 2,475 = 3,525, then 3,525 + 2,475 should be 6,000.

example.q: Without adding fully, which is bigger: 4,567 + 300 or 4,567 + 299?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers check change by adding back: if the bill is ₹1,275 and change ₹225, then ₹1,275 + ₹225 = ₹1,500 paid.

quiz.q: What is 5,010 + 95?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take away the extra 5

quiz.q: Which sign is correct? 2,468 + 1,000 ☐ 2,468 + 999
quiz.explain: Both add to 2,468, but 1,000 > 999.
quiz.mistake: Calculates fully and makes a slip

quiz.explain: Subtraction undoes addition: 3,579 − 1,234 = 2,345.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the related fact

quiz.explain: 2,340 is 10 more than 2,330, so the sum is 10 more: 6,900.

quiz.q: Ravi says 7,000 − 3,456 = 3,544. How can he check?
options: Add 3,544 + 3,456 and see if it makes 7,000
quiz.explain: Answer + number taken away = starting number. 3,544 + 3,456 = 7,000. ✓
quiz.mistake: Does not use addition to check

quiz.q: What is 3,600 − 99?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1 more instead of adding back

quiz.q: Which sign is correct? 6,000 − 250 ☐ 6,000 − 205
quiz.explain: Taking away more leaves less. 250 > 205, so 6,000 − 250 is smaller.
quiz.mistake: Thinks taking away more gives more

quiz.q: Check: is 8,203 − 4,567 = 3,636 correct?
quiz.explain: 3,636 + 4,567 = 8,203, so the subtraction is correct.

teach.ask: Gappu subtracted 7,000 − 2,345 and got 4,655. How can Gappu check without subtracting again?
teach.praise: 4,655 + 2,345 = 7,000! My answer is correct.
teach.nudge: What can you add to check a subtraction?

learn.hook: A big elephant can eat a huge pile of food every day! How much in a week? Multiply to find out!
points: When the same amount repeats every day or for every animal, multiply.
Break numbers into hundreds, tens and ones: 125 × 7 = 100 × 7 + 20 × 7 + 5 × 7.
To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it: 23 × 12 = 23 × 10 + 23 × 2.
Multiplying by 20 is like multiplying by 2 and then by 10.

example.q: A zoo elephant is given 125 kg of food each day. How much food does it get in 7 days?

learn.reallife: Zoo keepers plan how much food to buy for each animal for a week or a month.

quiz.q: Suppose an elephant drinks 150 litres of water a day. How much does it drink in 4 days?
A zoo elephant is given 125 kg of food each day. How much food is that in 7 days?
A tiger cub naps 15 hours a day. How many hours does it nap in 6 days?
Each safari jeep carries 6 visitors. 35 jeeps go out in a day. How many visitors go on safari?
What is 23 × 12?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 10 only and forgets the 2

quiz.q: A forest guard walks 14 km every day. How far does she walk in 12 days?
A ticket to the leopard safari costs ₹45. How much do 20 children pay altogether?
Which is the same as 16 × 25?
quiz.explain: 25 = 20 + 5, so 16 × 25 = 16 × 20 + 16 × 5. Each part must be multiplied by 16.
quiz.mistake: Splits 25 but forgets to multiply the 5 by 16

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find 23 × 12 but it looks too big! How can Gappu make it easier?
teach.praise: Wonderful! 23 × 10 = 230 and 23 × 2 = 46. Add them: 276. Gappu did it!
teach.nudge: Can Gappu split 12 into an easy 10 and a small part?

learn.hook: Some forest puzzles need two steps. Plan first, then solve one step at a time!
points: Read the problem and find what is asked at the end.
Find the hidden first step. For example, find the cost of all the tickets before finding the change.
Do the steps in order and write each answer.
Check: does the final answer make sense?

example.q: A forest has 3 lakes with 45 ducks on each. 28 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?

learn.reallife: A school trip to a national park needs two-step planning: total ticket cost, then change from the money collected.

games.title: Plan the steps
games.prompt: Put the steps in order: tickets cost ₹125 each. Find the change from ₹1000 for 6 tickets.

quiz.q: A viewing gallery has 4 rows of 25 seats. 63 seats are filled. How many seats are empty?
quiz.explain: Total seats: 4 × 25 = 100. Empty: 100 - 63 = 37.
quiz.mistake: Stops after finding the total seats

quiz.q: Safari tickets cost ₹30 for an adult and ₹15 for a child. How much do 2 adults and 3 children pay?
quiz.mistake: Uses the adult price for everyone or mixes up the numbers

quiz.q: 96 bananas are shared equally among 8 elephants. How many bananas does each elephant get?
A forest has 3 lakes with 45 ducks on each lake. 28 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?
quiz.explain: 3 × 45 = 135 ducks. 135 - 28 = 107 ducks left.
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake in the second step (gets 117)

quiz.q: A ranger buys 6 bags of seeds at ₹125 each. He pays with ₹1000. How much change does he get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change

quiz.q: A wildlife park gets 1500 visitors each day it is open. It is closed on Mondays. How many visitors come in one week?
quiz.explain: The park is open 7 - 1 = 6 days. 6 × 1500 = 9000 visitors.

quiz.q: 240 saplings are planted in rows of 12. How many rows are there?
In a camp, 5 grown-up elephants eat 150 kg each and 2 baby elephants eat 50 kg each in a day. How much food do they eat in all?
quiz.explain: Grown-ups: 5 × 150 = 750 kg. Babies: 2 × 50 = 100 kg. Total: 850 kg.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the change from ₹1000 after buying 6 tickets of ₹125. Gappu is stuck. What first?
teach.praise: Super! First find the cost (6 × 125 = 750), then the change (1000 - 750 = 250). Two steps done!
teach.nudge: What must Gappu find before the change? How much do all the tickets cost?

learn.hook: Fold a butterfly picture down the middle. Both halves match perfectly! That fold is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded.
Some shapes have one line of symmetry, some have many, and some have none.
A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A triangle with all sides equal has 3 lines of symmetry. A circle has endless lines of symmetry.
Letters like A, T and V have a standing (vertical) line of symmetry. B, C and E have a lying (horizontal) one. F, L, N and S have none.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does the letter H have?
steps: Fold H from top to bottom down the middle: the halves match.
Fold H from left to right across the middle: the halves match.

learn.reallife: Rangoli, the Taj Mahal from the front, leaves and many logos are symmetrical.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square can be folded in half 4 ways: up-down, left-right and along both corner-to-corner lines.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: It folds evenly only across the middle in two ways. A corner-to-corner fold does not make the halves match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry, like in a square

quiz.q: Which letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A folds down the middle into two matching halves. F, L and N do not match when folded.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any letter with straight lines is symmetrical

quiz.q: Which letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold makes the two halves of S match. H, T and E each have at least one line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks S is symmetrical because it looks the same when turned upside down

quiz.q: A triangle has all 3 sides equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: You can fold it from each corner to the middle of the opposite side. That is 3 lines.

quiz.q: Which letter has a lying (horizontal) line of symmetry, so its top half matches its bottom half?
quiz.explain: B folded from top to bottom matches. A, T and V have only a standing line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up standing (vertical) and lying (horizontal) lines

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
quiz.explain: H matches when folded down the middle and when folded across the middle. That is 2 lines.
quiz.mistake: Finds only one of the two folds

quiz.q: Which of these has the most lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes matching halves, so a circle has endless lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square has the most because it has 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded a paper heart down the middle and both halves matched! What is that fold line called?
teach.praise: Yes! When both halves match after folding, the fold is a line of symmetry. Gappu loves it!
teach.nudge: What happens to the two halves when Gappu folds? What do we call that line?

learn.hook: Drop some paint on paper, fold it, press and open. A butterfly appears! How?
points: Ink-blot design: put paint on one half, fold along the middle, press and open. The paint copies onto the other half like a mirror image.
The fold line is the line of symmetry of the design.
When folding a paper plane, the first middle fold is its line of symmetry. Both wings should match.
Place a mirror on the line of symmetry of half a picture and you see the whole picture.
A symmetrical plane flies straighter. If one wing is bigger, the plane turns or tips over.

example.q: Ritu folds a paper plane but one wing is bigger than the other. What will probably happen when she throws it?
steps: One side pushes on the air more than the other.
So the plane turns or tips instead of flying straight.
example.answer: It will turn or tip to one side

learn.reallife: Rangoli artists, ink-blot painters and paper-plane champions all use a fold line to make matching halves.

games.title: Make an ink-blot design
items: Fold a paper in half and open it
Fold it again along the same line
Open to see the matching halves

games.title: Planes and blots
items: The fold in an ink-blot design is a line of symmetry.
The two halves match across it.
A plane with one big and one small wing flies straight.
Unequal wings make it turn or tip.
A mirror on the line of symmetry shows the whole shape.
The mirror shows the missing half.
In an ink blot, the copy on the other half is exactly the same way round.
It is a mirror image, flipped left to right.
The middle fold of a paper plane helps make both wings equal.
It is the plane's line of symmetry.

quiz.q: In an ink-blot design, what is the fold line called?
quiz.explain: The fold line splits the design into two matching halves.

quiz.q: Paint is put on the left half and the paper is folded. Where does the copy appear?
options: On the right half, flipped like a mirror
quiz.explain: Folding presses the paint onto the other half as a mirror image.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the copy is not flipped

quiz.q: Why should both wings of a paper plane be the same?
quiz.explain: A symmetrical plane balances and flies straight.
quiz.mistake: Does not link symmetry to balance

quiz.q: Which fold is the line of symmetry of a paper plane?
options: The first fold down the middle
A fold at one wing tip
quiz.explain: The middle fold divides the plane into two equal halves.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fold that is not in the middle

quiz.q: Ankit places a mirror along the middle of half a butterfly drawing. What does he see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the other matching half, so the whole butterfly appears.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a mirror shows

quiz.q: An ink-blot design has 6 dots on the left half before folding (none on the fold). How many dots after opening?
quiz.explain: Each dot is copied to the right half: 6 + 6 = 12.

quiz.q: A plane drifts to the left every time. What is likely wrong?
quiz.explain: Unequal (not symmetrical) wings make a plane turn.

quiz.q: A mirror is placed on the line of symmetry of half the letter A. What letter do you see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the missing half, completing the A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror shows a different letter

teach.ask: Gappu wants to make a butterfly painting with matching wings. Explain how folding helps.
teach.praise: Paint one half, fold and press, and the wings match like a mirror. Beautiful!
teach.nudge: What does folding do to the paint on one half?

learn.hook: Put a mirror on half a picture and, like magic, the whole picture appears!
points: A mirror shows a flipped copy. Left becomes right and right becomes left.
If you know one half of a symmetrical shape, you can draw the other half like a mirror image.
Each point on one side is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner on the other side.
Fold paper, cut a shape on the fold and open it. You get a symmetrical shape!
In a mirror, b looks like d.

example.q: Half of a rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line, and no dots on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
steps: The right half is a mirror copy of the left half.

learn.reallife: Mehendi designs, kite patterns and paper cut-outs for Diwali use mirror halves.

games.title: Mirror magic
items: In a mirror, your right hand looks like a left hand.
A mirror flips left and right.
The letter b looks like d in a mirror held to its side.
The bump flips to the other side.
The mirror half of a shape can be a different size.
Mirror halves are exactly the same size and shape.
If you cut a half-heart on a fold and open the paper, you get a whole heart.
The fold is the line of symmetry.
The word MOM looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
M and O look the same flipped, and the word reads the same both ways.
The letter F looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
F faces the other way in the mirror.

items.text: Left half has 5 petals and none are on the line. The whole flower has ___ petals.
A half-shape is 3 squares wide. The full shape is ___ squares wide.
In a mirror held to the side, the letter d looks like ___.
A dot is 2 squares to the left of the mirror line. Its mirror dot is 2 squares to the ___.

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper in half and cuts out half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
quiz.explain: The fold is the line of symmetry. Opening it shows both matching halves joined: a whole heart.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the fold joins the two halves

quiz.q: In a mirror held to its side, what does the letter b look like?
quiz.explain: A mirror flips left and right. The bump of b moves to the left side, making it look like d.
quiz.mistake: Flips it upside down instead of left to right

quiz.q: A symmetrical rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line and none on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
quiz.explain: The right half is a mirror copy, so it has 7 dots too. 7 + 7 = 14.

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: M and O look the same when flipped, and MOM reads the same both ways. B, D, S, N and P do not.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one letter of the word

quiz.q: Which digit looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: 8 has a standing line of symmetry, so its mirror image is the same. 2, 4 and 7 face the other way.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture the digit flipped left to right

quiz.q: Arjun draws the left half of a symmetrical shape. It is 3 squares wide. How wide is the full shape?
quiz.explain: The right half is the same width as the left half. 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the half is already the whole shape

quiz.q: A dot is 4 squares to the left of a mirror line. Where is its mirror dot?
options: 4 squares to the right of the line
4 squares to the left of the line
8 squares to the right of the line
quiz.explain: A mirror dot is the same distance from the line but on the other side.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the distance instead of keeping it the same

quiz.q: Kabir stands 2 steps in front of a mirror. How far behind the mirror does his image seem to be?
quiz.explain: Your mirror image always seems to be the same distance behind the mirror as you are in front of it.

teach.ask: Gappu has half a butterfly drawing and a mirror. How can Gappu see or draw the whole butterfly?
teach.praise: Magic! Put the mirror on the line and the other half appears, the same but flipped. Gappu's butterfly is complete!
teach.nudge: What does a mirror do to a picture? How is the other half related to the first half?

topics.title: Holes and cuts: predict the pattern

learn.hook: Fold a paper twice, snip a corner, and open it. Will you get one hole or four?
points: Folding once makes 2 layers. A cut away from the fold makes 2 holes; a cut on the fold makes 1 hole.
Folding twice makes 4 layers. A cut in the middle (away from all folds) makes 4 holes.
A cut at the corner where both folds meet makes 1 hole in the centre of the paper.
A cut on just one folded edge (not the corner) makes 2 holes.
To get a square hole, fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner, the same distance along both folds.

example.q: A paper is folded twice. A small half-circle is cut on one folded edge, away from the corner. How many holes after opening?
steps: On a fold, the 4 layers pair up into 2 holes.

learn.reallife: Paper snowflakes and paper lanterns for Diwali are made by folding and cutting. The more folds, the more holes!

games.title: Cut and count the holes
pairs: 1 fold, cut away from the fold
2 folds, cut at the folded corner

games.title: Predict the cut
items: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, then 4.
One fold and a cut away from the fold gives 1 hole.
The cut goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes.
Cutting straight across the twice-folded corner can make a square hole.
The 4 corner pieces open into a square.
A half-circle cut on the fold opens into a full circle.
The two halves join at the fold.

quiz.q: A paper folded once has a half-circle cut on the fold. What do you see when you open it?
quiz.explain: The half-circle on the fold opens into one full circle.

quiz.q: A paper folded once has a small hole punched away from the fold. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The punch goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes.

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a hole punched in the middle, away from all folds. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: Two folds make 4 layers, so 4 holes.

quiz.q: A paper is folded twice and a quarter circle is cut at the corner where both folds meet. What do you get?
quiz.explain: The 4 quarter circles join into one circle in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each layer gives a separate hole

quiz.q: How many layers are there after folding a paper 3 times?
quiz.explain: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, 4, 8.

quiz.q: Maya wants a square hole in the centre. What should she do?
options: Fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner
Fold once and cut a circle
quiz.explain: A straight cut across the twice-folded corner opens into a square.

quiz.q: A paper is folded once. On the fold, Ravi cuts a rectangle 1 cm wide (from the fold) and 2 cm long (along the fold). What hole does he get?
quiz.explain: The 1 cm width doubles to 2 cm when opened, so the hole is 2 cm by 2 cm, a square.

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a small notch cut on one folded edge, not at the corner. How many notches or holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The 4 layers pair up across the fold, making 2 holes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every cut on 4 layers gives 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded paper twice and punched one hole in the middle. Gappu expected 1 hole but got 4. Explain.
teach.praise: Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes! Now I can predict.
teach.nudge: How many layers does the paper have after two folds?

learn.hook: The word AMBULANCE is written back to front on the van. Why? Look in a car's mirror!
points: Place a mirror on a shape. If the shape and its reflection make the same shape, the mirror is on a line of symmetry.
Digits like 0, 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror held beside them.
A mirror also reverses the order of digits. So only numbers like 88, 101 and 808 look the same in the mirror.
AMBULANCE is written in mirror writing on the front of the van so drivers ahead can read it in their rear-view mirror.
You can try mirror writing in any script: write each letter flipped, starting from the other side.

example.q: Does 18 look the same in a mirror held beside it?
steps: 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror.
But the mirror swaps their order: 18 looks like 81.
So 18 does not look the same.

learn.reallife: Next time you see an ambulance, look at the front. The writing is reversed for the mirrors of cars in front!

games.title: Looks the same in a mirror held beside it?

items.text: AMBULANCE is reversed so drivers read it in their ___.
In a mirror, 18 looks like ___.
The digit ___ looks the same in a mirror.
Mirror writing starts from the ___ side.

quiz.q: Which number looks exactly the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 8 and 0 look the same in a mirror, and 808 reads the same from both ends.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the mirror reverses the order

quiz.q: Why is AMBULANCE written in mirror writing on the van?
options: So only children can read it
So drivers ahead can read it in their mirrors
quiz.explain: A rear-view mirror flips the writing back to normal.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how mirrors flip words

quiz.q: How does the number 18 look in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 1 and 8 stay the same, but the order is reversed: 81.

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: W and O look the same in a mirror, and WOW reads the same both ways.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with non-symmetric letters

quiz.q: Hema puts a mirror across a heart shape. The heart and its reflection make the same heart. Where is the mirror?
quiz.explain: When a mirror shows the same shape, it is on the line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the mirror to symmetry

quiz.q: Which number made of 1s and 0s looks the same in a mirror?
quiz.explain: 1001 reads the same from both ends, and 1 and 0 look the same in a mirror.

quiz.q: Which of these digits does NOT look the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 3 flips and faces the other way. 0, 8 and 1 stay the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all digits stay the same

quiz.q: Sunil writes his name in mirror writing. How should he write?
options: Flip each letter and start from the other side
quiz.explain: Mirror writing flips each letter left to right and reverses the order.
quiz.mistake: Thinks mirror writing is upside down

teach.ask: Gappu wrote 18 and looked in the mirror. Gappu saw 81 and got confused. Explain.
teach.praise: The mirror swaps the order! Only numbers like 88 or 808 look the same.
teach.nudge: What does a mirror do to the order of digits?

topics.title: Symmetry of regular shapes on a dot grid

learn.hook: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry. Coincidence? Let's check other shapes!
points: A regular shape has all sides equal and all angles equal.
Regular triangle: 3 lines of symmetry. Square: 4. Regular pentagon: 5. Regular hexagon: 6.
For a regular shape, the number of lines of symmetry equals the number of sides.
A rectangle that is not a square has only 2. A shape like a kite has 1.
On a dot grid, draw a shape and then test each possible fold line to find its lines of symmetry.

example.q: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
steps: For a regular shape, lines = sides.

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, road signs and honeycombs often use regular shapes because they look balanced from every side.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
quiz.explain: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
quiz.explain: Regular shapes have as many lines of symmetry as sides.

quiz.q: A square has 4 sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: 2 lines through the middles of sides and 2 diagonals: 4.

quiz.q: Which shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: A rectangle folds in half across and along, but not on its diagonals.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry

quiz.q: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.

quiz.q: On a dot grid, Sara draws a kite shape. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: A kite folds into matching halves only along its long middle line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it has 2 like a rectangle

quiz.q: Which is true for regular shapes?
options: Lines of symmetry = double the sides
Lines of symmetry = number of sides
They have no lines of symmetry
quiz.explain: Triangle 3, square 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6.

quiz.q: How many more lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have than a regular triangle?

teach.ask: Gappu found a regular pentagon tile and wants to know how many ways it can be folded into matching halves. Explain.
teach.praise: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so 5 lines of symmetry!
teach.nudge: What is the link between sides and lines of symmetry in regular shapes?

learn.hook: Look at a bathroom wall. The same tile design repeats again and again. Can you find the smallest piece that repeats?
points: A tile pattern repeats a basic unit again and again.
To continue the pattern, find the unit and repeat it in the same way.
A tile can be slid (moved without turning), flipped (like a mirror) or turned (rotated) to make patterns.
A quarter turn rotates a tile by one right angle. Four quarter turns bring it back to the start.

example.q: A border goes ▲▼▲▼▲▼. What is the repeating unit, and which move changes ▲ into ▼?
steps: ▼ is ▲ flipped upside down (or turned half a turn).
example.answer: Unit ▲▼; a flip or half turn

learn.reallife: Sarees, bangles, temple floors and school walls all have tile patterns made by sliding, flipping or turning one design.

quiz.q: In the pattern ■●■●■●, what is the repeating unit?
quiz.explain: ■● repeats again and again.
