quiz.q: A tile is moved to the right without turning or flipping. What is this move called?
quiz.explain: Moving without turning is a slide.

quiz.q: A tile with an arrow → becomes ← . Which single move could do this?
quiz.explain: Flipping like a mirror changes → to ←. A half turn does too.

quiz.q: How many quarter turns bring a tile back to how it started?
quiz.explain: 4 quarter turns make a full turn.

quiz.q: What comes next? ▲▲▼▲▲▼▲▲
quiz.explain: The unit is ▲▲▼, so after ▲▲ comes ▼.

quiz.q: In ⭐🌙🌙⭐🌙🌙, how many shapes are in the repeating unit?
quiz.explain: ⭐🌙🌙 has 3 shapes.

quiz.q: A tile is turned a quarter turn each time: ↑ then →. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each quarter turn moves the arrow one right angle clockwise: ↑, →, ↓, ←.

quiz.q: A floor border uses the unit 🟥🟨🟨. How many 🟨 tiles are in 4 units?
quiz.explain: Each unit has 2 yellow tiles. 4 × 2 = 8.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to tile a wall border with a pattern. Explain how to make one using a single tile.
teach.praise: I picked a unit and slid, flipped or turned it again and again. My border is ready!
teach.nudge: What do you repeat, and what moves can you use?

learn.hook: Bees build honeycombs with hexagons that fit perfectly. Why not circles?
points: Tessellation means covering a surface with shapes that leave no gaps and do not overlap.
Squares, rectangles, regular triangles and regular hexagons tessellate on their own.
Circles and regular pentagons leave gaps, so they do not tessellate on their own.
Some tiles in a shop are symmetrical, some are not. Look for a line of symmetry in each tile design.
You can join shapes to make a new tile that tessellates, or design your own tile with cut-outs or a rangoli kit.

example.q: Can circular tiles cover a floor without gaps?
steps: There are curved gaps between them.

learn.reallife: Look at floors, footpaths and walls. Paver blocks and tiles fit together like a puzzle with no gaps!

games.title: Tessellation facts
items: Tiles in a tessellation may overlap.
Hexagons fit together with no gaps.
Two regular triangles joined make a shape that also tessellates.
They make a rhombus, which tessellates.
Every tile design in a shop is symmetrical.
Some designs have no line of symmetry.

quiz.q: What does tessellation mean?
options: Covering a surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps
quiz.explain: Tessellating shapes fit together completely.

quiz.q: Which shape does NOT tessellate on its own?
quiz.explain: Circles leave gaps between them.

quiz.q: Which shape do bees use in honeycombs?
quiz.explain: Regular hexagons fit together with no gaps.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that leaves gaps

quiz.q: Two regular triangles are joined side to side. Does the new tile tessellate?
quiz.explain: They make a rhombus, which fits with copies of itself.

quiz.q: A tile shows a flower with 4 equal petals. Is it symmetrical?
quiz.explain: A flower with 4 equal petals has lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Does not look for a fold line

quiz.q: Which is true about a regular pentagon?
options: It leaves gaps when tiled alone
quiz.explain: Regular pentagons do not fit together without gaps.

quiz.q: A floor is covered by 6 rows of 8 square tiles with no gaps. How many tiles?
Leena makes her own tile using a rangoli kit. What must be true for it to tile a floor?
options: Copies fit together with no gaps or overlaps
quiz.explain: A tessellating tile fits with its copies, leaving no gaps.

teach.ask: Gappu wants round tiles for the classroom floor. Explain why that may be a problem.
teach.praise: Round tiles leave gaps! Squares or hexagons fit perfectly.
teach.nudge: What happens between circles when you put them side by side?

topics.title: Floor patterns and the catty wall

learn.hook: Cut a bump from one side of a square and stick it on the opposite side. You get a cat-shaped tile that still fits!
points: A floor pattern is made by repeating one tessellating tile again and again.
Catty-wall trick: cut a piece from one side of a square and slide it to the opposite side.
The new tile has a funny shape (like a cat), but copies still fit together with no gaps.
The area stays the same, because nothing was thrown away: the piece only moved.
If the piece is not slid exactly to the opposite side, the tiles will not fit.

example.q: Raghav cuts a small triangle from the bottom of a square tile and sticks it on the top. Will copies fit together?
steps: The bump on top matches the gap at the bottom of the tile above.
So copies fit with no gaps or overlaps.

learn.reallife: Artists make animal-shaped tiles, like birds and fish, using this trick. Some famous tiles look like lizards!

games.title: Make a catty-wall tile
items: Cut a shape from one side
Slide the piece to the opposite side
Repeat the tile to cover the wall

games.title: Catty-wall facts
items: Sliding the cut piece to the opposite side keeps the tile tessellating.
The bump fits the gap of the next tile.
The new tile has a bigger area than the square.
The piece was only moved, so the area stays the same.
You can stick the piece anywhere and it will still fit.
It must go exactly opposite where it was cut.
A floor pattern repeats one tile again and again.
If made by cutting and sliding, they fit together.

quiz.q: In the catty-wall trick, where does the cut piece go?
quiz.explain: The piece is slid to the opposite side so the tiles still fit.

quiz.q: After the catty-wall trick, how does the tile's area compare with the square's?
quiz.explain: Nothing is added or removed; a piece is only moved.

quiz.q: Why do the new cat-shaped tiles still fit together?
options: The bump on one side fills the gap on the next tile
quiz.explain: Each bump matches a gap, so there are no gaps or overlaps.
quiz.mistake: Does not see bumps and gaps match

quiz.q: What is a floor pattern made by?
options: Repeating one tile with no gaps
quiz.explain: A floor pattern repeats a tessellating tile.

quiz.q: Tanu cuts a piece from the left side of a square and sticks it on the TOP. What may happen?
options: The tiles may not fit together
quiz.explain: The piece must slide to the opposite side (right). Moving it elsewhere breaks the fit.

quiz.q: A wall needs 5 rows of 7 catty tiles. How many tiles?
A square tile has area 16 small squares. After the catty-wall trick, what is its area?
quiz.explain: Moving a piece does not change the area.
quiz.mistake: Adds or takes away the piece

quiz.q: Which shape is the best start for a catty-wall tile?
quiz.explain: Squares tessellate, so a cut-and-slide square still tessellates.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that does not tessellate

teach.ask: Gappu wants a wall full of cat-shaped tiles that fit with no gaps. How can Gappu make the tile?
teach.praise: Cut a bit from a square and slide it to the opposite side! Meow, it fits!
teach.nudge: Where must the cut piece go so the tiles still fit?

learn.hook: Look closely at a butterfly, a peepal leaf or a hibiscus flower. Nature loves symmetry!
points: Many living things are symmetrical: a butterfly's wings match, and many leaves match on both sides of the middle vein.
Some leaves are not symmetrical, like a torn leaf or a leaf with uneven sides.
Sort leaves into symmetrical and non-symmetrical by folding them along the middle vein.
Flowers with equal petals, like a 5-petal hibiscus, can have several lines of symmetry.
Use leaves and flowers dipped in paint to make prints for designs and greeting cards.

example.q: A flower has 5 equal petals evenly spread. How many lines of symmetry might it have?
steps: Like a regular pentagon, a line can go through each petal.

learn.reallife: On a nature walk, collect fallen leaves and flowers. Fold them to test symmetry, then print them on a Diwali card!

games.title: Nature symmetry
items: Its body is the line of symmetry.
The middle vein of a leaf is often its line of symmetry.
The two halves match across it.
Leaf prints can be used to make greeting cards.
Paint the leaf and press it on paper.
A flower with 4 equal petals has no line of symmetry.
It has lines of symmetry through the petals.

quiz.q: Which part of a butterfly is its line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: The body divides the butterfly into two matching halves.
quiz.mistake: Picks a part on one side

quiz.q: How can you test if a leaf is symmetrical?
options: Fold it along the middle vein and see if the halves match
quiz.explain: If the halves match when folded, it is symmetrical.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to test

quiz.q: Which is most likely NOT symmetrical?
options: A leaf torn on one side
quiz.explain: The torn side no longer matches the other side.

quiz.q: A flower has 6 equal petals evenly spread. How many lines of symmetry can it have?
quiz.explain: Like a regular hexagon, it has 6 lines of symmetry.

quiz.q: Riya collects 12 leaves. 9 are symmetrical. How many are not?
To make a leaf print card, what should you do?
options: Paint a leaf and press it on paper
quiz.explain: Painting and pressing makes a print.

quiz.q: A leaf print is made on one half of a folded card and the card is pressed shut. What appears on the other half?
options: A mirror image of the print
quiz.explain: The wet paint copies as a mirror image, like an ink blot.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect it with ink-blot designs

quiz.q: Which animal shows symmetry when seen from the front?
quiz.explain: A tiger's face has matching left and right halves.

teach.ask: Gappu found a leaf on a nature walk. How can Gappu check if it is symmetrical, and what can Gappu make with it?
teach.praise: Fold along the middle vein: the halves match! Now I will print it on a card.
teach.nudge: How do you test the leaf, and what can you make from it?

learn.hook: Your birthday is coming! How many days to wait? The calendar knows!
points: A week has 7 days. A year has 12 months.
April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year). All the other months have 31 days.
A year has 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.
The same day of the week comes again every 7 days. If 1 June is a Monday, so are 8, 15, 22 and 29 June.
To count days to a date in the next month, count to the end of this month, then add the days of the next month.

example.q: Today is 28 March. Aisha's birthday is on 5 April. How many days does she have to wait?
steps: March has 31 days. From 28 March to 31 March is 31 - 28 = 3 days.
Then 5 more days to reach 5 April.

learn.reallife: We use calendars to plan holidays, mark exams, count days to Diwali and remember birthdays.

games.title: Calendar facts
items: February gets an extra day, the 29th.
If 1 June is a Monday, then 8 June is also a Monday.
In a year that is not a leap year, February has 28 days.
Only a leap year gives February 29 days.

quiz.q: How many days are there in March?
quiz.explain: March is one of the months with 31 days.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up March with a 30-day month

quiz.q: In a year that is not a leap year, how many days does February have?
quiz.explain: February is the shortest month. It has 28 days, and 29 only in a leap year.
quiz.mistake: Gives the leap-year number of days

quiz.q: How many days are there in a year that is not a leap year?
quiz.explain: An ordinary year has 365 days. A leap year has 366.

quiz.q: 1 June is a Monday. What day is 8 June?
quiz.explain: 8 June is 7 days after 1 June. The day of the week repeats every 7 days, so it is Monday again.

quiz.q: Today is Friday. What day will it be 3 days from today?
quiz.explain: Count on: Saturday (1), Sunday (2), Monday (3).
quiz.mistake: Counts today as one of the 3 days

quiz.q: How many weeks are there in 28 days?
quiz.explain: Each week has 7 days. 28 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 7 from 28 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Today is 28 March. Aisha's birthday is on 5 April. How many days does she have to wait?
quiz.explain: 28 March to 31 March is 3 days, then 5 more days to 5 April. 3 + 5 = 8 days.

quiz.q: Which of these months has 30 days?
quiz.explain: April has 30 days. May, January and August each have 31 days.

teach.ask: Today is 25 May and Gappu's party is on 2 June. Gappu thinks it's 7 days away. How do we count?
teach.praise: Yes! May has 31 days: 25 to 31 is 6 days, then 2 more makes 8 days. Gappu is excited!
teach.nudge: How many days does May have? Count to the end of May first.

learn.hook: Some children have a birthday on 29 February. They get a real birthday only once in 4 years!
points: A leap year comes every 4 years. It has 366 days because February gets a 29th day.
An ordinary year has 365 days.
2024 was a leap year. Add 4 for the next ones: 2028, 2032. Take away 4 for earlier ones: 2020, 2016.

Many festivals and special days come in fixed months: Republic Day in January, Independence Day in August, Teachers' Day in September, Gandhi Jayanti in October, Children's Day in November, Christmas in December.

example.q: 2024 is a leap year. Which are the next two leap years?

learn.reallife: Calendars help us plan holidays and festivals. Your school calendar marks Republic Day and Independence Day every year.

quiz.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
quiz.explain: A leap year has one extra day, 29 February: 365 + 1 = 366.

quiz.q: 2024 was a leap year. Which year is the next leap year?
quiz.explain: Leap years come every 4 years: 2024 + 4 = 2028.

quiz.q: 2024 was a leap year. Which year was the leap year before it?
How often does a leap year come?
quiz.explain: One year in every 4 is a leap year.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every other year is a leap year

quiz.q: How many days does February have in a leap year?
quiz.explain: In a leap year, February has 29 days.

quiz.q: In which month do we celebrate Independence Day?
quiz.explain: Independence Day is on 15 August.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with Republic Day

quiz.q: Children's Day is on 14 November. In which month is it?
quiz.explain: 14 November is in November.

quiz.q: How many leap years are there from 2021 to 2032 (both included)?
quiz.explain: 2024, 2028 and 2032: 3 leap years.

teach.ask: Gappu was born on 29 February 2024. When will Gappu's next real birthday be? Explain.
teach.praise: 29 February comes only in leap years, every 4 years. My next real birthday is in 2028!
teach.nudge: How often does 29 February come?

learn.hook: If today is Wednesday, what was the day before yesterday? And what will be the day after tomorrow?
points: Yesterday is 1 day before today. The day before yesterday is 2 days before.
Tomorrow is 1 day after today. The day after tomorrow is 2 days after.
The same date moves to a later weekday in the next month. A 31-day month moves it 3 days on; a 30-day month 2 days; a 28-day February 0 days.
Example: 1 January is a Monday. January has 31 days, so 1 February is 3 days later in the week: Thursday.

example.q: Today is Wednesday. What is the day after tomorrow? What was the day before yesterday?
steps: Tomorrow: Thursday. Day after tomorrow: Friday.
Yesterday: Tuesday. Day before yesterday: Monday.

learn.reallife: Planning a trip 'the day after tomorrow' or remembering a test 'the day before yesterday' uses these words every day!

items.text: Tomorrow is ___.
Yesterday was ___.
The day after tomorrow is ___.
The day before yesterday was ___.

games.title: Days the weekday moves on to the next month

quiz.q: Today is Monday. What day is the day after tomorrow?
quiz.explain: Tomorrow is Tuesday, the day after is Wednesday.

quiz.q: Today is Friday. What was the day before yesterday?
quiz.explain: Yesterday was Thursday; the day before that was Wednesday.

quiz.q: 1 March is a Sunday. March has 31 days. What day is 1 April?
quiz.explain: 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days. Sunday + 3 days = Wednesday.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the weekday stays the same

quiz.q: 1 April is a Wednesday. April has 30 days. What day is 1 May?
quiz.explain: 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 days. Wednesday + 2 = Friday.

quiz.q: In a year that is not a leap year, 1 February is a Tuesday. What day is 1 March?
quiz.explain: February has exactly 28 days = 4 weeks, so the weekday stays the same.

quiz.q: Today is the 10th. What date was the day before yesterday?
Today is the 27th. What date will the day after tomorrow be?
How many days does the weekday move on from 1 July to 1 August? (July has 31 days.)
quiz.explain: 31 days is 4 weeks and 3 days, so it moves on 3 days.

teach.ask: Gappu knows 1 January is a Monday and wants to find the day on 1 February. Explain the trick.
teach.praise: 31 days is 4 weeks and 3 days, so Monday + 3 = Thursday!
teach.nudge: How many full weeks are in 31 days, and how many days are extra?

learn.hook: Your juice box says 'Best before 6 months from manufacture'. When does it expire?
points: To find who is older, compare birth years first, then months, then dates. The earlier date is older.
Find how much older by counting days, months or years between the birth dates.
To find a future birthday's date, keep the day and month and change the year: born 14 June 2016, 10th birthday is 14 June 2026.
A pack shows a manufacturing (MFD) date and an expiry (EXP) date. Count the months and days between them to find how long it is good for.

example.q: A biscuit packet was made on 10 March 2026. It expires on 10 September 2026. How long is it good for?
steps: From 10 March to 10 September: count months.
April, May, June, July, August, September: 6 months.

learn.reallife: Always check the expiry date on medicines and food packets before using them!

items.q: MFD Jan, EXP July (same date): months
Born 3 June and 11 June: days apart

games.title: Who is older?
items: A child born in 2015 is older than one born in 2017.
Someone born on 20 March is older than someone born on 12 March of the same year.
12 March comes first, so that person is older.
A 10th birthday of a child born 5 May 2016 is 5 May 2026.
Food should be eaten after the expiry date.
It may be unsafe after expiry.
MFD means the date the product was made.

quiz.q: Asha was born on 12 March 2016. Ravi was born on 20 March 2016. Who is older and by how many days?
quiz.explain: Same year and month; 12 comes before 20. 20 − 12 = 8 days. Asha is older.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger date is older

quiz.q: Rohit was born in 2014 and his sister in 2019. How many years older is Rohit?
Meena was born on 14 June 2016. On what date is her 10th birthday?
quiz.explain: Keep the date and month, add 10 to the year: 2016 + 10 = 2026.

quiz.q: A juice packet: MFD 1 January, EXP 1 April (same year). How many months is it good for?
quiz.explain: January to April is 3 months.

quiz.q: A medicine: MFD 5 May, EXP 25 May. How many days is it good for?
Bread is made on 3 August. It stays good for 5 more days after that. What is the last good date?
quiz.explain: 3 + 5 = 8 August.

quiz.q: A packet says 'MFD: March 2026. Best before 6 months from MFD.' When does it expire?
quiz.explain: 6 months after March: Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep. So September 2026.

quiz.q: Who is the oldest? Ali: 5 Jan 2016, Bina: 30 Dec 2015, Chetan: 1 Feb 2016.
quiz.explain: Bina was born in 2015, the earliest year.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the date number

teach.ask: Gappu found a cake box: MFD 10 June, EXP 10 August. Gappu wants to know how long it is good for and if it is safe on 15 August.
teach.praise: 2 months, and 15 August is after the expiry, so I will not eat it!
teach.nudge: How many months from MFD to EXP, and is 15 August before or after expiry?

learn.hook: Baisakhi, Chaitra, Muharram, Ramzan... Different communities in India use their own calendars too!
points: Besides the English calendar, communities use other calendars, like Hindu, Islamic and Sikh calendars, with their own month names and New Year.
Hindu month Chaitra usually falls around March–April. Baisakh (Vaisakh) falls around April–May; Baisakhi is in mid-April.
The Islamic calendar follows the moon. Its months, like Muharram and Ramzan, come about 10 to 11 days earlier every year in the English calendar.
Amavasya (new moon) and Purnima (full moon) repeat in a pattern: each comes about once every 29 to 30 days, about 15 days apart.
Many festivals are fixed by the moon: Diwali is on an Amavasya; Holi and Guru Nanak Jayanti are on a Purnima.

example.q: Purnima was on 5 March. About when will the next Purnima be?
steps: Purnima comes about every 29 to 30 days.
5 March + about 29 or 30 days → about 3 or 4 April.

learn.reallife: Ask your grandparents which calendar months they use for festivals. You may learn new month names!

games.title: Moon and calendars
items: Purnima comes about once a month.
Amavasya and Purnima are about 15 days apart.
The Islamic calendar's months fall on the same English dates every year.
They come about 10 to 11 days earlier each year.
Diwali is celebrated on an Amavasya.
It is on the new moon night.
Every community in India uses only the English calendar.
Many also use their own calendars.

quiz.q: What is Purnima?
quiz.explain: Purnima is the full moon night.

quiz.q: What is Amavasya?
options: New moon, when we cannot see the moon
quiz.explain: On Amavasya the moon is not seen.

quiz.q: About how many days are there from one Purnima to the next?
quiz.explain: The moon's cycle takes about 29 to 30 days.
quiz.mistake: Gives the gap between Purnima and Amavasya

quiz.q: About how many days after Amavasya does Purnima come?
quiz.explain: They are about half a moon cycle apart: about 15 days.

quiz.q: Around which English months does the Hindu month Chaitra usually fall?
quiz.explain: Chaitra usually begins in March and ends in April.

quiz.q: Why do Islamic months move to different English dates each year?
options: The Islamic calendar follows the moon
quiz.explain: A moon year is about 354 days, about 11 days shorter than 365.

quiz.q: Diwali falls on which kind of night?
quiz.explain: Diwali is on Amavasya, which is why lamps light up the dark night.

quiz.q: A Purnima is on 10 May. About when is the next Amavasya?
quiz.explain: Amavasya comes about 15 days after Purnima: 10 + 15 = 25 May.

teach.ask: Gappu's grandma says the next festival is on the next Purnima. Today is Purnima. When should Gappu expect it?
teach.praise: Purnima comes about every 29 to 30 days, so the festival is about a month away!
teach.nudge: How long does the moon take to become full again?

topics.title: How many hours in a day?

learn.hook: You sleep, eat, study and play. Do all your activities add up to one full day?
points: A day has 24 hours.
From 6 am to 6 pm is 12 hours. From 6 am to the next morning's 6 am is 24 hours.
Add up the hours spent on each activity to see how a day is used.
If you know the hours for some activities, subtract from 24 to find the rest.

example.q: Mohan sleeps 9 hours, is at school 7 hours, plays 2 hours and studies 2 hours. How many hours are left for other things?

learn.reallife: A railway timetable runs all 24 hours, and some shops are open 24 hours a day!

games.title: Day facts
items: That is one full turn of the Earth.
From 6 am to 6 pm is 24 hours.
From 9 pm to 9 am is 12 hours.
Count: 9 pm to 9 am is 12 hours.
All the activities in a day add up to 24 hours.
Sleep, school, play and the rest fill the day.
Sleeping from 10 pm to 6 am is 6 hours.

quiz.q: How many hours are there in a day?
quiz.explain: A full day has 24 hours.

quiz.q: How many hours from 6 am to 6 pm?
quiz.explain: 6 am to 12 noon is 6 hours, then 6 more to 6 pm: 12.

quiz.q: How many hours from 6 am today to 6 am tomorrow?
quiz.explain: That is one full day, 24 hours.

quiz.q: Pinky sleeps from 9 pm to 6 am. How many hours does she sleep?
quiz.explain: 9 pm to 12 midnight is 3 hours; 12 to 6 am is 6 hours. 3 + 6 = 9.

quiz.q: Ravi sleeps 10 hours and is at school 6 hours. How many hours are left in the day?
quiz.mistake: Gives the hours used instead of left

quiz.q: Sita's day: sleep 9 h, school 7 h, homework 2 h, play 2 h, meals 2 h. How many hours is that?
In Sita's day, how many hours are not listed?
A shop is open from 8 am to 8 pm. How many hours is it open?
quiz.explain: 8 am to 12 noon is 4 h; 12 noon to 8 pm is 8 h. 4 + 8 = 12.

teach.ask: Gappu wonders why the day feels so short. Help Gappu add up the hours in a day.
teach.praise: Sleep, school, play and more add up to 24 hours. Now I can plan my day!
teach.nudge: How many hours does a day have, and how do you find time left?

topics.title: How long does it take? Time durations

learn.hook: School starts at 8:00 am and ends at 1:30 pm. How long are you in school? Let's count the time!
points: am is for times from midnight to noon (morning). pm is for times from noon to midnight (afternoon and night).
1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 hours = 120 minutes.
To find how long, count on: first to the next full hour, then the hours, then the minutes.
To find the end time, add the time taken to the start time. If minutes reach 60, change them into 1 hour.

example.q: A cricket match on TV goes from 2:40 pm to 4:10 pm. How long is it?

learn.reallife: We work out how long a train journey takes, or how long we can play before dinner.

items.text: 2 hours = ___ minutes
3:15 pm + 2 hours = ___
90 minutes = 1 hour ___ minutes

quiz.q: School starts at 8:00 am and ends at 1:30 pm. How long is the school day?
quiz.explain: 8:00 am to 12:00 noon is 4 hours. 12:00 to 1:30 pm is 1 hour 30 minutes. Total: 5 hours 30 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Counts from 8 to 1 wrongly by forgetting that 12 comes before 1

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in 2 hours?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 × 60 = 120 minutes.

quiz.q: A film starts at 3:15 pm and lasts 2 hours. When does it end?
quiz.explain: Add 2 hours to 3:15 pm: 4:15 pm, then 5:15 pm. It is still afternoon, so pm.
quiz.mistake: Changes pm to am, or adds 2 minutes

quiz.q: Arjun eats breakfast at 7 o'clock in the morning. How do we write this time?
quiz.explain: Morning times before noon use am. So it is 7:00 am.

quiz.q: A cricket match on TV goes from 2:40 pm to 4:10 pm. How long is it?
quiz.explain: 2:40 to 3:00 is 20 minutes, 3:00 to 4:00 is 60 minutes, 4:00 to 4:10 is 10 minutes. 20 + 60 + 10 = 90.

quiz.q: Riya sleeps at 9:30 pm and wakes up at 6:30 am. How long does she sleep?
quiz.explain: 9:30 pm to 12:00 midnight is 2 hours 30 minutes. Midnight to 6:30 am is 6 hours 30 minutes. Together: 9 hours.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 9:30 - 6:30 and forgets the time goes past midnight

quiz.q: How many hours and minutes is 90 minutes?
quiz.explain: 60 minutes make 1 hour. 90 - 60 = 30. So 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 hour is 40 minutes or divides by 10

quiz.q: A clock shows 10:45. What time will it be 20 minutes later?
quiz.explain: 10:45 + 15 minutes = 11:00. 5 more minutes makes 11:05.

teach.ask: Gappu's train leaves at 2:40 pm and arrives at 4:10 pm. Gappu did 410 - 240 = 170 minutes. Is that right?
teach.praise: Aha! An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on: 20 + 60 + 10 = 90 minutes!
teach.nudge: How many minutes are in an hour? Try counting on to 3:00 first.

learn.hook: A digital clock shows 07:45. Your school bell rings at 08:00. How many minutes to go?
points: A digital clock shows hours, then minutes: 07:45 means 7 hours and 45 minutes, which is 7:45.
Look for am or pm on the clock to know if it is morning or evening.
A schedule lists events with start and end times. Each event starts when the one before ends.
Add the time taken to a start time to find when an event ends.
Many small tasks take about 5 minutes: brushing teeth, tying shoes, packing a bag.

example.q: Assembly 8:00 am to 8:20 am. Period 1 lasts 40 minutes after that. When does period 1 end?

learn.reallife: Railway stations, phones and microwave ovens all show digital time. Schedules keep schools and trains on time!

quiz.q: A digital clock shows 07:45 am. What time is it?
quiz.explain: 07:45 means 7 hours 45 minutes; am means morning.

quiz.q: A digital clock shows 09:05 pm. Which is correct?
quiz.explain: 09:05 is 9 hours 5 minutes; pm means evening or night.

quiz.q: Assembly ends at 8:20 am. Period 1 is 40 minutes long. When does it end?
quiz.explain: 8:20 + 40 minutes = 8:60, which is 9:00.

quiz.q: Lunch starts at 12:30 pm and lasts 30 minutes. Next is art for 45 minutes. When does art end?
quiz.explain: Lunch ends 1:00 pm. 1:00 + 45 minutes = 1:45 pm.

quiz.q: Which task takes about 5 minutes?
quiz.explain: Brushing teeth takes a few minutes.

quiz.q: The bus comes at 7:50 am. The digital clock shows 07:38. How many minutes until the bus comes?
quiz.explain: 50 − 38 = 12 minutes.

quiz.q: Sports starts at 3:15 pm and lasts 50 minutes. When does it end?
quiz.explain: 15 + 50 = 65 minutes = 1 hour 5 minutes. 3:15 + 50 min = 4:05 pm.

quiz.q: Tying both shoes takes about 2 minutes. Packing your bag takes about 5 minutes. How long for both?
quiz.explain: 2 + 5 = 7 minutes.

teach.ask: Gappu's tuition starts at 4:40 pm and lasts 35 minutes. Gappu wants to know when it ends. Explain.
teach.praise: 40 + 35 = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes, so it ends at 5:15 pm!
teach.nudge: What happens when the minutes go past 60?

learn.hook: Tick, tock! The train leaves at 7:05. Can you read the clock and not miss it?
points: The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
The long hand moves from one number to the next in 5 minutes. So at 4 it shows 20 minutes, at 9 it shows 45 minutes.
Between two numbers there are 5 small marks. Each small mark is 1 minute.
Quarter past 6 is 6:15. Half past 6 is 6:30. Quarter to 7 is 6:45.
We write minutes with two digits: 7 o'clock and 5 minutes is 7:05.

example.q: The short hand is between 4 and 5. The long hand is 2 small marks after the 7. What time is it?
steps: Hour: the short hand has passed 4, so the hour is 4.

learn.reallife: We read clocks to catch the school bus, start a cricket match or know when our favourite show begins.

items.q: Long hand on 3: how many minutes past?
Long hand on 6: how many minutes past?
Long hand on 8: how many minutes past?
Long hand on 11: how many minutes past?
Long hand 3 small marks after 2: minutes past?
Long hand on 1: how many minutes past?

quiz.q: The short hand is just past 3 and the long hand is on 4. What time is it?
quiz.explain: The short hand shows 3 o'clock has passed. The long hand on 4 means 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. So it is 3:20.
quiz.mistake: Reads the long hand number as the minutes (3:04) or mixes up the hands

quiz.q: The long hand points to 9. How many minutes past the hour is it?
quiz.explain: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand. 9 × 5 = 45 minutes.

quiz.q: What time is 'quarter past 6'?
quiz.explain: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes. Quarter past 6 is 15 minutes after 6: 6:15.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up quarter past and quarter to

quiz.q: What time is 'half past 11'?
quiz.explain: Half an hour is 30 minutes. Half past 11 is 11:30.

quiz.q: The clock shows 8:50. How else can we say this time?
quiz.explain: 8:50 is 10 minutes before 9:00, so it is 10 minutes to 9.
quiz.mistake: Uses the hour that has passed instead of the coming hour

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in 1 hour?
quiz.explain: The long hand goes all the way round once in 60 minutes. That is 1 hour.
quiz.mistake: Thinks an hour has 100 minutes, like a metre has 100 cm

quiz.q: The short hand is between 4 and 5. The long hand is 2 small marks after the 7. What time is it?
quiz.explain: The hour is 4. The long hand at 7 means 35 minutes, and 2 more marks make 37. So 4:37.
quiz.mistake: Writes the 7 and the 2 side by side

quiz.q: The train leaves at 7 o'clock and 5 minutes. How do we write this time?
quiz.explain: Minutes are written with two digits. 5 minutes is written as 05, so 7:05.

teach.ask: Gappu sees the long hand on 4 and says it is 4 minutes past. Is Gappu right?
teach.praise: Thank you! Each number is 5 minutes for the long hand, so 4 means 20 minutes. Gappu reads clocks now!
teach.nudge: How many minutes does the long hand take to go from one number to the next?

learn.hook: Bunty says the clock shows 12:15, but it is really 3 o'clock. What went wrong?
points: The short hand is the hour hand. The long hand is the minute hand.
Mixing up the hands gives a wrong time: hour hand on 3 and minute hand on 12 is 3:00, not 12:15.
Read the hour from the number the short hand has just passed, not the one it is moving towards.
At 7:30 the hour hand is halfway between 7 and 8. It is still 7-something, not 8.
To read a clock: (1) find the short hand and read the hour, (2) find the long hand and count minutes in 5s, (3) add the extra small marks.

example.q: The short hand is just before 8. The long hand is on 10. What time is it?
steps: The short hand has passed 7 and not reached 8: hour = 7.

learn.reallife: Train stations and schools run on time only if everyone reads clocks correctly!

games.title: How to read a clock
items: Read the hour it has just passed

games.title: Spot the mistake
items: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12: the time is 3:00.
Short hand on 3, long hand on 12: the time is 12:15.
That mixes up the two hands.
At 7:30 the hour hand points halfway between 7 and 8.
It moves slowly between the numbers.
Short hand just before 8, long hand on 10: the time is 8:50.
The hour is still 7, so it is 7:50.
The long hand on 6 shows 30 minutes.

quiz.q: The short hand is on 3 and the long hand is on 12. What time is it?
quiz.explain: Short hand gives the hour (3); long hand on 12 means 0 minutes.

quiz.q: The short hand is halfway between 6 and 7 and the long hand is on 6. Bunty says it is 7:30. What is the right time?
quiz.explain: Short hand between 6 and 7 → hour 6. Long hand on 6 → 30 minutes. 6:30.

quiz.q: The short hand is just before 8. The long hand is on 10. What time is it?
quiz.explain: The hour hand has not reached 8, so it is still 7. 10 × 5 = 50 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Reads the hour it is moving towards

quiz.q: Which hand shows the hour?
quiz.explain: The short hand points to the hour.

quiz.q: The long hand is on 4. How many minutes past the hour is it?
quiz.explain: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes.

quiz.q: At 9:45, where is the hour hand?
options: Most of the way from 9 to 10
quiz.explain: 45 minutes is three-quarters of an hour, so the hour hand is three-quarters of the way to 10.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hour hand stays on the number

quiz.q: Rina says the time is 4:12 because the short hand is on 12 and the long hand is on 4. What is the right time?
quiz.explain: Short hand on 12 → hour 12. Long hand on 4 → 20 minutes. 12:20.

quiz.q: The long hand is 3 small marks after the 2. How many minutes past the hour?
quiz.explain: 2 × 5 = 10, plus 3 small marks = 13 minutes.

teach.ask: Gappu read a clock as 12:15 when it was 3:00. Teach Gappu how to read a clock correctly.
teach.praise: Short hand for hours, long hand for minutes in 5s. Now I read clocks perfectly!
teach.nudge: Which hand shows the hour, and how do you count the minutes?

learn.hook: A times grid has lost its row and column numbers! Only the answers are left. Can you find the missing factors?
points: In a times grid, each box = row factor × column factor.
If you know a box and one factor, divide to find the other: box 42 with row factor 6 → column factor 42 ÷ 6 = 7.
Use two boxes in the same row or column as clues: 12 and 18 in a row share a factor, like 2, 3 or 6.
In a number grid, look for three numbers in a line that make a true multiplication or division sentence, like 6, 7, 42.

example.q: Row A has boxes 12 and 18. Row B has 30 and 45. Column 1's factor is 6. Find the other factors.

learn.reallife: Number puzzles in newspapers use the same thinking: use clues to find missing numbers!

quiz.q: A box shows 42 and its row factor is 6. What is its column factor?
Row factor 8, box 72. What is the column factor?
Row A has 12 and 18. Column 1's factor is 6. What is row A's factor?
Row A's factor is 2 and its second box is 18. What is column 2's factor?
Row B is in column 1 (factor 6) with box 30. What is row B's factor, and what is its box in column 2 (factor 9)?
Two single-digit factors multiply to 56. What are they?
quiz.explain: 7 × 8 = 56, and both are single digits.
quiz.mistake: Picks a pair that is not single digits

quiz.q: Which three numbers in a grid make a true sentence?
A box shows 63. Its column factor is 7. What is the row factor?

teach.ask: Gappu's times grid lost its labels. One box shows 48 and its row factor is 6. Help Gappu find the column factor.
teach.praise: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, and 6 × 8 = 48 checks it!
teach.nudge: If you know the product and one factor, how do you find the other?

learn.hook: 10 × 10 is 10 tens, which is 100. What is 65 × 10? Just put a zero at the end!
points: Multiplying by 10 makes tens: 7 × 10 = 7 tens = 70.
A 2-digit number × 10: 65 × 10 = 65 tens = 650. The digits move one place to the left and a 0 fills the ones place.
Pictures help: 6 bundles of 10 sticks show 6 × 10 = 60.

example.q: What is 47 × 10?

learn.reallife: ₹10 notes: 23 notes of ₹10 make ₹230. Counting tens is quick!

quiz.q: What is 10 × 10?
What is 65 × 10?
A picture shows 8 bundles of 10 sticks. Which multiplication matches?
quiz.explain: 8 groups of 10 is 8 × 10 = 80.

quiz.q: How many tens are there in 470?
A school bus has 10 rows of 4 seats. How many seats?
Arjun has 23 notes of ₹10. How much money?
What happens to the digits of 58 when you multiply by 10?
options: They move one place left and a 0 comes in the ones place
quiz.explain: 58 × 10 = 580: 5 becomes hundreds, 8 becomes tens.

quiz.q: Which picture shows 10 × 10?
quiz.explain: 10 rows of 10 make 100 dots, which is 10 × 10.
quiz.mistake: Picks a picture with only 10 dots

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 34 × 10 is 3410. Help Gappu.
teach.praise: 34 tens is 340! Just one zero comes at the end.
teach.nudge: How many tens is 34 × 10?

learn.hook: You know the 10s and the 5s. Put them together and you get the 15s!
points: Split 15 into 10 + 5. Then 15 × n = 10 × n + 5 × n.
Each times-15 answer = times-10 answer + times-5 answer, in the same row.
The 15s table ends in 5, 0, 5, 0... just like the 5s table.

example.q: Find 15 × 7 by splitting.

learn.reallife: 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour. 4 × 15 = 60 minutes, a full hour!

quiz.q: What is 15 × 6?
Which is the same as 15 × 8?
quiz.explain: Split 15 into 10 and 5, and multiply each by 8.

quiz.q: In the 15s table, each answer is how much more than the one before?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 15.

quiz.q: What comes next? 60, 75, 90, ?
Which number is in the times-15 table?
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number ending in 5 or 0 is in it

quiz.q: A bus trip takes 15 minutes. How many minutes for 4 trips?
quiz.explain: 15 × 4 = 60 minutes = 1 hour.

quiz.q: How is 15 × 10 related to 10 × 10 and 5 × 10?
quiz.mistake: Writes the numbers side by side

teach.ask: Gappu forgot the 15s table. Show Gappu how to build 15 × 7 from tables Gappu knows.
teach.praise: 10 × 7 = 70 and 5 × 7 = 35. Together 105! I can build any 15s fact.
teach.nudge: Which two easy tables make up the 15s table?

learn.hook: 11 × 6? That's 10 × 6 + 1 × 6 = 66. 12 × 6? 60 + 12 = 72. Every table from 11 to 20 is easy now!
points: In the same way, times-13 = times-10 + times-3, and so on up to times-19 = times-10 + times-9.

example.q: Find 13 × 6 and 18 × 4.

learn.reallife: Shops sell eggs in dozens (12). 12 × 5 = 60 eggs in 5 dozen!

quiz.q: What is 11 × 9?
What is 12 × 6?
Which is the same as 14 × 7?
quiz.explain: Split 14 into 10 and 4.

quiz.q: What is 16 × 5?
What is 19 × 4?
Times-12 is times-10 plus which table?
A carton has 12 eggs. How many eggs in 8 cartons?
What is 17 × 3?

teach.ask: Gappu knows tables only up to 10. How can Gappu find 13 × 7?
teach.praise: 70 + 21 = 91! Splitting 13 into 10 and 3 makes it easy.
teach.nudge: How can you split 13, and what do you do with each part?

learn.hook: 6 × 14 is just double 3 × 14. Doubling makes big tables from small ones!
points: If one number doubles, the product doubles: 6 × 14 = double (3 × 14) = double 42 = 84.
The times-14 table is the times-7 table doubled: 14 × 5 = double (7 × 5) = double 35 = 70.
Other tables made by doubling: 8 from 4, 12 from 6, 16 from 8, 18 from 9, 20 from 10.
Odd tables like 13, 15, 17 and 19 cannot be made by doubling a whole-number table.

example.q: Find 14 × 6 using the 7s table.

learn.reallife: If one bag of rice costs ₹45, two bags cost double: ₹90. Doubling is everywhere!

games.title: Which table doubles to make it?

quiz.explain: 6 is double 3, so double 42 = 84.
14 is double 7, so double 63 = 126.

quiz.q: Which table can be made by doubling the times-9 table?
quiz.explain: Double 9 is 18.

quiz.q: Which table can NOT be made by doubling a whole-number table?
quiz.explain: 15 is odd, so it is not double any whole number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every table can be doubled from another

quiz.explain: Double 56 = 112.

quiz.q: What is 14 × 4?

quiz.explain: 12 is double 6, so double 36 = 72.

quiz.q: Ravi says, 'To get the 20s table, double the 10s table.' Is he right?
quiz.explain: 20 × n = double (10 × n). E.g. 20 × 3 = double 30 = 60.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the doubling link

teach.ask: Gappu wants the times-14 table but only knows the times-7 table. Explain how to get 14 × 8.
teach.nudge: How is 14 related to 7, and what happens to the product?

points: To multiply by 40, multiply by 4 and then by 10: 24 × 40 = 24 × 4 × 10 = 96 × 10 = 960.
Multiply two multiples of 10 using the basic fact, then add two zeros: 50 × 60 = 5 × 6 × 100 = 3000.
Count the zeros: 30 × 40 has 2 zeros in the factors, so the answer 1200 ends in 2 zeros (after 3 × 4 = 12).

example.q: Find 35 × 20.

learn.reallife: A cinema has 40 rows of 25 seats: 25 × 40 = 1000 seats!

quiz.q: What is 24 × 40?
What is 50 × 60?
quiz.explain: 5 × 6 = 30, then add two zeros: 3000.

quiz.q: What is 70 × 80?
Which is the same as 32 × 20?
quiz.explain: 20 = 2 × 10, so multiply by 2 then by 10.

quiz.q: A hall has 40 rows of 25 chairs. How many chairs?
What is 30 × 90?
quiz.explain: 3 × 9 = 27, then two zeros: 2700.

quiz.q: What is 18 × 50?
Which product is the biggest?
quiz.mistake: Picks the one with the biggest single factor

teach.ask: Gappu must find 60 × 40 and is scared of big numbers. Show Gappu the easy way.
teach.praise: 6 × 4 = 24 and two zeros make 2400. Not scary at all!
teach.nudge: Which basic fact helps, and how many zeros do you add?

learn.hook: A museum train has 23 coaches with 14 seats each. How many seats? Split and multiply!
points: Split both numbers into tens and ones: 23 × 14 = (20 + 3) × (10 + 4).
Multiply each part (partial products): 20 × 10 = 200, 20 × 4 = 80, 3 × 10 = 30, 3 × 4 = 12.
Add the partial products: 200 + 80 + 30 + 12 = 322.
A partial-product table puts tens and ones on the sides and the products inside.
The ones digit of a product depends only on the ones digits: 23 × 47 ends in 1, because 3 × 7 = 21.

example.q: A museum has 16 vintage buses. Each bus has 32 seats. How many seats?

learn.reallife: Railways work out seats on trains using big multiplications like coaches × seats per coach.

quiz.q: What is 23 × 14?
Which partial products make 15 × 12?
quiz.explain: Split both: (10 + 5) × (10 + 2) gives four parts.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only tens with tens and ones with ones

quiz.q: What is 15 × 12?
A train has 18 coaches with 24 seats each. How many seats?
A museum shows 14 old cars. Each has 4 wheels and 1 spare. How many wheels and spares in all?
quiz.explain: Each car has 4 + 1 = 5. 14 × 5 = 70.

quiz.q: Without multiplying fully, what is the ones digit of 23 × 47?
quiz.explain: 3 × 7 = 21, so the product ends in 1. (23 × 47 = 1081.)

quiz.q: A coach carries 42 passengers. How many passengers in 13 coaches?
Which product ends in 6?
quiz.mistake: Does not use the ones digits

teach.ask: Gappu must work out 21 × 13 for the museum bus seats. Show Gappu the splitting method.
teach.praise: 200 + 60 + 10 + 3 = 273! Four small multiplications and one addition.
teach.nudge: How do you split both numbers, and what do you do with the parts?

learn.hook: 250 visitors and each museum train coach holds 48. How many coaches are needed?
points: To divide by a 2-digit number, find how many times it fits using multiplication facts you can build.
Try a guess and check: 48 × 5 = 240, 48 × 6 = 288. 250 is between, so 5 coaches with 10 left over.
The remainder must be less than the divisor.
Decide what the remainder means: 10 people left over need one more coach, so 6 coaches.

example.q: 365 days are put into groups of 30 days. How many full groups are there, and how many days are left?

learn.reallife: Bus and train planners divide the number of passengers by the seats per coach every day.

games.title: Remainder facts
items: The remainder must be less than the divisor.
Otherwise one more group could be made.
If 10 people are left over, no extra coach is needed.
They also need a seat, so one more coach.

quiz.q: What is 96 ÷ 12?
250 people, 48 per coach. How many FULL coaches and how many people left?
quiz.mistake: Gives a remainder bigger than the divisor

quiz.q: Using the above, how many coaches are needed so that everyone travels?
quiz.explain: 5 full coaches carry 240; the 10 left need a 6th coach.

quiz.q: What is 807 ÷ 24?
What is 144 ÷ 12?
Which is a correct division?
quiz.explain: 12 × 8 = 96. 100 − 96 = 4, which is less than 12.
quiz.mistake: Gives a remainder that is too big

quiz.q: A museum has 360 tickets to put in bundles of 15. How many bundles?
75 children go in vans of 12. How many vans are needed?
quiz.explain: 12 × 6 = 72. 3 children left need a 7th van.

teach.ask: Gappu divided 100 by 12 and wrote '7 remainder 16'. What is wrong? Fix it.
teach.praise: 16 is more than 12, so one more group fits! The answer is 8 remainder 4.
teach.nudge: Can the remainder be bigger than the number you divide by?

learn.hook: 27 × 100 = 2700. 11 × 200 is double 11 × 100. Patterns make big products easy!
points: Multiplying by 100 makes hundreds: 27 × 100 = 27 hundreds = 2700.
Multiply by 200, 300, 500, 800 using a fact and place value: 6 × 300 = 18 hundreds = 1800.
Doubling pattern: 11 × 200 is double 11 × 100 (2200 is double 1100).
Related products: 44 × 10 = 22 × 20 = 440. Halve one number (44 → 22) and double the other (10 → 20).
Making one number 4 times smaller and the other 4 times bigger keeps the product too: 16 × 100 = 4 × 400 = 1600.

example.q: Is 16 × 100 the same as 4 × 400?
steps: 16 is 4 times 4, and 400 is 4 times 100: one up, one down.

learn.reallife: In a bank, ₹100 and ₹200 notes are counted in bundles. 27 notes of ₹100 make ₹2700!

quiz.q: What is 27 × 100?
quiz.explain: 27 hundreds = 2700.

quiz.q: What is 6 × 300?
quiz.explain: 6 × 3 = 18, so 18 hundreds = 1800.
200 is double 100, so the product doubles: 2200.

quiz.q: Which is equal to 44 × 10?
quiz.explain: Halve 44 to 22 and double 10 to 20: same product, 440.

quiz.q: Which is equal to 16 × 100?
What is 5 × 800?
quiz.explain: 5 × 8 = 40, so 40 hundreds = 4000.

quiz.q: A shop sells 9 boxes of 500 beads. How many beads?

teach.ask: Gappu says 12 × 200 is 12 × 100 + 100. Help Gappu see the doubling pattern.
teach.praise: 200 is double 100, so 12 × 200 is double 1200 = 2400!
teach.nudge: How is 200 related to 100, and what happens to the product?

topics.title: Bigger multiplication and dividing by 10 and 100

learn.hook: 237 × 28? Split 28 into 20 and 8. And 600 ÷ 100? Just remove two zeros!
points: Dividing by 10 removes one zero from the end: 450 ÷ 10 = 45. Dividing by 100 removes two: 600 ÷ 100 = 6.
Divide by 20 or 200 using related facts: 800 ÷ 20 = 80 ÷ 2 = 40; 1200 ÷ 200 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
Word problems: 900 kg of rice in 100 kg sacks → 900 ÷ 100 = 9 sacks.

example.q: A transport company has 125 trucks. Each carries 32 boxes. How many boxes?

learn.reallife: Rice mills pack grain in 50 kg or 100 kg sacks. Dividing by 10 and 100 tells how many sacks they need!

quiz.q: What is 237 × 28?
What is 600 ÷ 100?
quiz.explain: Dividing by 100 removes two zeros: 6.

quiz.q: What is 800 ÷ 20?
What is 1200 ÷ 200?
quiz.explain: 12 hundreds ÷ 2 hundreds = 6.

quiz.q: 900 kg of rice is packed in 100 kg sacks. How many sacks?
A trader has 480 bananas in bunches of 12. How many bunches?
₹3000 is shared equally among 100 children. How much does each get?
What is 145 × 12?

teach.ask: Gappu must share 1600 sweets equally into boxes of 200. Show Gappu a quick way.
teach.praise: 16 hundreds ÷ 2 hundreds = 8 boxes!
teach.nudge: How many hundreds are in 1600 and in 200?

topics.title: Transport word problems and Chinnu's coins

learn.hook: Chinnu wants to pay ₹750 using only ₹200 notes. How many notes, and will he get change?
points: Multi-step problems: decide for each step whether to multiply (equal groups) or divide (sharing or grouping).
To pay with one kind of note, divide: 750 ÷ 50 = 15 notes exactly.
If it does not divide exactly, you need one more note and you get change: 750 ÷ 200 = 3 r 150, so 4 notes (₹800) and ₹50 change.
Someone pays exactly when the amount divides with no remainder.
Match vehicles to how many they carry when full: bicycle 1–2, auto-rickshaw 3, car 4–5, bus about 50, train hundreds or more.

example.q: Chinnu pays ₹750 using only ₹20 notes. How many notes, and how much change?

learn.reallife: School trips, bus fares and train tickets all need careful step-by-step maths!

quiz.q: A train has 12 coaches with 72 seats each. 650 tickets are sold. How many seats are empty?
A school trip: 180 children and 12 teachers go in buses of 48. How many buses are needed?
Tickets cost ₹25 each. A class of 36 buys tickets. They pay with ₹100 notes. How many notes?
Chinnu pays ₹750 using only ₹200 notes. How many notes must he give?
quiz.explain: 3 notes = ₹600, not enough. 4 notes = ₹800.
quiz.mistake: Gives 3 notes, which is not enough

quiz.q: Chinnu gives 4 notes of ₹200 for a ₹750 bill. How much change does he get?
quiz.mistake: Uses the remainder as the change

quiz.q: How many ₹5 coins make exactly ₹750?
Who pays ₹750 EXACTLY? Asha uses only ₹50 notes. Babu uses only ₹100 notes.
quiz.explain: 750 ÷ 50 = 15 exactly. 750 ÷ 100 = 7 r 50, so Babu needs 8 notes and gets change.
quiz.mistake: Does not check for a remainder

quiz.q: A brick kiln makes 450 bricks a day. A truck carries 900 bricks. How many trucks are needed for 6 days of bricks?

teach.ask: Gappu has only ₹200 notes and must pay ₹750 for a boat trip. How many notes, and what change?
teach.praise: 3 notes are not enough, so 4 notes (₹800) and I get ₹50 back!
teach.nudge: Are 3 notes enough? How much change do you get with one more?

learn.hook: The ticket to the transport museum costs ₹75. Which notes and coins will you give?
points: ₹1 = 100 paise.
₹5.50 means 5 rupees and 50 paise. The dot separates rupees from paise.
We have notes like ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200 and ₹500, and coins like ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20.
To count money, start with the biggest notes, then add the smaller ones.
There are many ways to make the same amount. ₹75 = ₹50 + ₹20 + ₹5.

example.q: Kabir has four ₹20 notes and three ₹5 coins. How much money does he have?

learn.reallife: We count money when buying tickets, snacks at the station or souvenirs at a museum shop.

quiz.q: How many paise make ₹1?
quiz.explain: 1 rupee is the same as 100 paise.

quiz.q: Joseph has three ₹500 notes and two ₹100 notes. How much money does he have?
How many ₹10 coins make ₹100?
How do we write 5 rupees and 50 paise?
quiz.explain: Rupees go before the dot and paise after it: ₹5.50.

quiz.q: The museum ticket costs ₹75. Which set of money makes exactly ₹75?
quiz.mistake: Does not add up each set carefully

quiz.q: How many rupees is 250 paise?
quiz.explain: 100 paise = ₹1. 250 paise = ₹2 and 50 paise = ₹2.50.

quiz.q: Riya must pay ₹700 using only ₹500 and ₹100 notes. What is the smallest number of notes she can use?
quiz.explain: One ₹500 note and two ₹100 notes make ₹700. That is 1 + 2 = 3 notes.

quiz.q: Kabir has four ₹20 notes and three ₹5 coins. How much money does he have?
Chinnu wants to pay ₹350 using only ₹50 notes. How many notes does he need?
quiz.explain: 350 ÷ 50 = 7, because 7 × 50 = 350. He pays exactly, with no change.

teach.ask: Gappu found 150 paise in the piggy bank. Gappu thinks it is ₹150. Is that right?
teach.praise: Oh! 100 paise make ₹1, so 150 paise is ₹1.50, not ₹150. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many paise make one rupee?

learn.hook: At the museum shop you buy toy trains and postcards. The shopkeeper gives you a bill. Can you check it?
points: A bill lists each item, how many (quantity), the price of one (rate) and the amount.
Amount = quantity × rate. 3 toy trains at ₹45 each = 3 × 45 = ₹135.
Add all the amounts to get the total.
Always check a bill. Shopkeepers can make mistakes too!
Change = money given - total.

example.q: Bill: 5 pencils at ₹6 each and 2 erasers at ₹5 each. What is the total?

learn.reallife: Grocery shops, restaurants and railway ticket counters all give bills.

items.text: Qty 4, Rate ₹25, Amount ₹___
Qty 3, Rate ₹45, Amount ₹___
Qty 2, Rate ₹120, Amount ₹___
Total ₹385, paid ₹500, change ₹___

games.title: Is the bill right?
items: Multiply how many by the price of one.
Change from ₹500 for a ₹385 bill is ₹125

quiz.q: Meena buys 3 toy trains at ₹45 each. What is the amount?
quiz.explain: Amount = quantity × rate = 3 × ₹45 = ₹135.

quiz.q: A bill has 5 pencils at ₹6 each and 2 erasers at ₹5 each. What is the total?
quiz.explain: Pencils: 5 × 6 = ₹30. Erasers: 2 × 5 = ₹10. Total = ₹40.

quiz.q: On a bill, what does 'rate' mean?
quiz.explain: Rate is the price of one item. Amount = quantity × rate.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rate with amount or quantity

quiz.q: Apples cost ₹120 per kg. Aisha buys 2 kg. What is the amount?
A bill line says: Qty 4, Rate ₹25. What should the amount be?
quiz.explain: 4 × 25 = 100. So the amount is ₹100.

quiz.q: A bill says 3 postcards × ₹40 = ₹130. What should the correct amount be?
quiz.explain: 3 × 40 = 120, so the bill should say ₹120. The shopkeeper made a mistake.

quiz.q: At the transport museum, adult tickets cost ₹50 and child tickets cost ₹20. What is the bill for 2 adults and 3 children?
quiz.explain: Adults: 2 × 50 = ₹100. Children: 3 × 20 = ₹60. Total: ₹160.
quiz.mistake: Adds one adult and one child ticket only (₹70)

quiz.q: Harpreet's bill total is ₹385. She pays with a ₹500 note. How much change should she get?

teach.ask: Gappu bought 4 toy cars at ₹25 each. The bill says ₹125. How can Gappu check the bill?
teach.praise: Well done! 4 × 25 = 100, so the bill should be ₹100. Gappu saved ₹25!
teach.nudge: How do we find the amount from the number of cars and the price of one?

learn.hook: Saving for a model train? Sharing a taxi fare? Money maths helps every day!
points: Add to find a total cost. Subtract to find what is left or how much more is needed.
Multiply when the same price repeats. Divide to share money equally.
When adding rupees and paise, 100 paise make ₹1: ₹10.50 + ₹4.50 = ₹15.00.
To compare deals, find the price of one item in each.

example.q: Joseph has ₹200. A toy bus costs ₹135. How much money will he have left?

learn.reallife: Families share expenses for a trip, save money every week and compare prices before buying.

games.title: Which operation?
items: Savings of ₹25 a week for 8 weeks
How much more is needed to buy a bicycle
Cost of a samosa and a juice together

quiz.q: Joseph has ₹200. A toy bus costs ₹135. How much money will he have left?
₹360 is shared equally among 4 friends. How much does each get?
Which is cheaper per pen: a pack of 3 pens for ₹30 or 1 pen for ₹12?
options: Both cost the same per pen
quiz.explain: In the pack each pen costs 30 ÷ 3 = ₹10, which is less than ₹12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ₹12 is cheaper because it is a smaller number than ₹30

quiz.q: A toy train ride ticket costs ₹85. How much do 6 tickets cost?
Meena saves ₹25 every week. How much will she save in 8 weeks?
A bicycle costs ₹1250. Arjun has ₹875. How much more money does he need?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two amounts instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Harpreet buys 2 samosas at ₹15 each and 1 juice for ₹25. She pays with ₹100. How much change does she get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change, or counts only one samosa

teach.ask: Gappu wants to share ₹120 equally with 2 friends, so 3 in all. How much should each get?
teach.praise: Great! ₹120 ÷ 3 = ₹40 each. Fair sharing makes good friends!
teach.nudge: How many people share the money, counting Gappu? What operation shares equally?

topics.title: Asking the right question and recording answers

learn.hook: 'Do you like school?' or 'Which subject do you like most: Maths, English, EVS or Hindi?' Which question gives better data?
points: A good survey question is clear and gives the information you need.
Giving choices helps: 'Which is your favourite subject: Maths, English, EVS or Hindi?'
Record answers quickly with short codes: M for Maths, E for English, V for EVS, H for Hindi.
Data can be shown as a long list of codes or as a table of counts. A table is much easier to read.
Choose the way of showing data that answers questions fastest.

example.q: Codes recorded: M E M V H M E M V M. How many chose Maths?

learn.reallife: Teachers, shopkeepers and the government run surveys to plan things like school timetables, stock and new roads.

games.title: Good survey question?
items: Which fruit do you like most: mango, banana or apple?
How do you come to school: walk, bus, cycle or car?
How many brothers and sisters do you have?

games.title: Count the codes (M E V H)

items.q: M M E V M: how many M?
E E H V E: how many E?
V H V V M V: how many V?
H M H E: how many H?
M E M V H M E M: total answers

quiz.q: Which is the best survey question to find classmates' favourite sport?
options: Which sport do you like most: cricket, football, kabaddi or badminton?
quiz.explain: It is clear and gives choices, so the answers can be counted.

quiz.q: Riya records favourite subjects as M, E, V, H. What does V stand for?
quiz.explain: V is the short code for EVS.

quiz.q: Codes: M E M V H M E. How many children chose English (E)?
quiz.explain: E appears 2 times.

quiz.q: Codes: M E M V H M E. How many children answered in all?
quiz.explain: There are 7 codes, one per child.

quiz.q: Which way of showing data is easier to read: a long list of codes, or a table of counts?
quiz.explain: A table shows each total at once, so we do not need to count again.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare ways of showing data

quiz.q: Why do we use short codes when recording answers?
quiz.explain: Codes save time when many people answer.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the use of codes

quiz.q: Codes: M M E V M H M. Which subject is the favourite?
quiz.explain: M appears 4 times, the most.

quiz.q: Raju asks 'Do you like food?' Everyone says yes. What is wrong with his question?
options: It does not tell which food they like
quiz.explain: A yes/no question cannot show favourites. He should list food choices.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any question gives useful data

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the class's favourite fruit. Help Gappu ask a good question and record the answers.
teach.praise: I asked 'Mango, banana or apple?', wrote codes and made a table. Mango wins!
teach.nudge: What makes a good question, and how will you record and show the answers?

learn.hook: Which fruit does your class love most? Don't guess. Ask everyone and count. That's data!
points: Data is information we collect, like answers to a question or things we count.
We can collect data by asking people (a survey) or by watching and counting.
Tally marks help us count fast: 4 lines and a 5th line across make a bundle of 5.
We put the counts in a table so it is easy to read and compare.
From a table we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

example.q: In a survey, 12 children chose mango, 8 chose banana and 5 chose apple. How many children took part, and which fruit is the favourite?
steps: The biggest count is 12, for mango.

learn.reallife: Teachers collect data on attendance. Cricket scorers keep data on runs and wickets.

games.title: Data facts
items: A survey means asking people questions and noting their answers.
That is one way to collect data.
In tally marks, the 5th line goes across the other 4.
Guessing is a good way to collect data.
We must ask or count to get real data.
A table makes data easier to read.
Counts are neatly lined up to compare.
If mango has 12 votes and apple has 5, apple is more popular.
12 is more than 5, so mango is more popular.

quiz.q: Arjun's tally for red cars has 2 bundles of five and 3 more lines. How many red cars did he count?
quiz.explain: 2 bundles of five = 10. 3 more lines make 13.

quiz.q: In a survey, 12 children chose mango, 8 chose banana and 5 chose apple. How many children took part?
quiz.explain: 12 + 8 + 5 = 25 children.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the fruits

quiz.q: In the same survey (mango 12, banana 8, apple 5), which fruit is the favourite?
quiz.explain: Mango has the biggest count, 12.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit with the smallest count

quiz.q: How many more children chose mango (12) than apple (5)?
quiz.explain: 12 - 5 = 7 more children chose mango.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Riya wants to know how her classmates come to school. What is the best way to collect this data?
options: Ask each child and make tally marks
Guess from looking at the gate once
Count the bicycles at her home
quiz.explain: Asking every child and keeping a tally gives correct, complete data.
quiz.mistake: Thinks asking one person or guessing is enough

quiz.q: A table of favourite colours shows Red 9, Blue 6, Green 9, Yellow 4. Which two colours got the same number of votes?
quiz.explain: Red and Green both have 9 votes.

quiz.q: Kabir counted vehicles passing his school: 14 cars, 23 bikes and 9 buses. How many vehicles did he count?
quiz.explain: 14 + 23 + 9 = 46 vehicles.

quiz.q: In Kabir's count (14 cars, 23 bikes, 9 buses), how many fewer buses than bikes were there?
quiz.explain: 23 - 9 = 14 fewer buses.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the favourite sweet of all the birds in the forest. How should Gappu find out?
teach.praise: Yes! Ask everyone, count with tally marks and write it in a table. Gappu will find the favourite sweet!
teach.nudge: Should Gappu just guess? What should Gappu do with each answer?

learn.hook: Tall bars, short bars! A bar graph lets you compare data in one quick look.
points: A bar graph uses bars to show data. A taller (or longer) bar means a bigger number.
Read the number at the end of each bar using the scale on the side.
The scale can go up in 1s, 2s, 5s or 10s. Check it before reading!
We can use a bar graph to find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

example.q: A bar graph shows rangoli kits sold: Monday 4, Tuesday 7, Wednesday 3, Thursday 6. Which day sold the most, and how many were sold in all?

learn.reallife: TV news shows bar graphs of rainfall, cricket runs per over and votes.

games.title: Bars from shortest to tallest
games.prompt: Rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. Order from fewest to most.

games.title: Bar graph facts
items: A taller bar shows a bigger number.
The height of a bar shows the amount.
The scale on a bar graph must always go up in 1s.
It can go up in 2s, 5s, 10s and so on.
Two bars of the same height show the same number.
The shortest bar shows the most popular choice.
The tallest bar shows the most popular choice.
If each line stands for 2, a bar reaching the 6th line shows 12.

quiz.q: A bar graph shows rangoli kits sold: Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. On which day were the most kits sold?
quiz.explain: Tuesday has the tallest bar, 7 kits.
quiz.mistake: Picks the day with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Rangoli kits sold were Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. How many more kits were sold on Tuesday than on Wednesday?
quiz.explain: 7 - 3 = 4 more kits on Tuesday.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two bars instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Rangoli kits sold were Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. How many kits were sold in the 4 days altogether?
A bar graph of favourite games shows Cricket 15, Kabaddi 10, Kho-kho 5, Football 10. Which two games have bars of the same height?
quiz.explain: Kabaddi and Football both have 10 votes, so their bars are the same height.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the bar values carefully

quiz.q: On a bar graph, each line on the scale stands for 2 students. A bar reaches the 6th line. How many students does it show?
quiz.explain: 6 lines × 2 students = 12 students.
quiz.mistake: Reads the line number without using the scale

quiz.q: In the favourite games graph (Cricket 15, Kabaddi 10, Kho-kho 5, Football 10), which game is liked the least?
quiz.explain: Kho-kho has the shortest bar, only 5 votes.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tallest bar instead of the shortest

quiz.q: What does a taller bar in a bar graph show?
quiz.explain: The taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bar height has no meaning

quiz.q: A bar graph shows rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. How many rainy days were there in July and August together?
quiz.explain: 15 + 12 = 27 rainy days.
quiz.mistake: Finds the difference instead of the total

teach.ask: Gappu sees a bar graph of fruits but doesn't know how to read it. What should Gappu look at?
teach.praise: Thank you! Taller bars mean more, and the scale tells the exact number. Gappu can read graphs now!
teach.nudge: What does a taller bar mean? Where does Gappu read the number?

topics.title: Colourful golas: reading and making pictographs

learn.hook: The gola-wala sold rose, mango, khus and orange golas. Which flavour should he buy more syrup for?
points: To make a picture chart, colour or draw one symbol for each group of data, using the key.
Read a pictograph: count symbols and multiply by the key value.
The row with the most symbols shows the most popular item; the fewest shows the least.
Use data to decide: buy more of the most popular flavour.
Data can be split into groups, like boys and girls, to compare them separately.

example.q: Using the gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2), how many mango golas were sold?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers look at what sells most before ordering new stock. That is using data to decide!

items.text: 10 golas need ___ symbols.
8 golas need ___ symbols.
14 golas need ___ symbols.
1 gola needs ___ symbol.

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. Which flavour was sold the most?
quiz.explain: Mango has the most symbols (6).

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. How many rose golas were sold?
quiz.explain: 4 symbols × 2 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts symbols without using the key

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. Which flavour was sold the least?
quiz.explain: Khus has only 2 symbols.

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. The gola-wala can buy only one big bottle of syrup. Which flavour should he choose?
quiz.explain: Mango sells the most, so it is the best choice.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the data to decide

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. How many more mango golas than khus golas were sold?
quiz.explain: Mango 12, khus 4. 12 − 4 = 8.

quiz.q: Boys bought 5 rose golas and girls bought 9. Using 🍧 = 1, how many symbols for girls?
quiz.explain: Each symbol is 1 gola, so 9 symbols.

quiz.q: Boys: rose 5, mango 7. Girls: rose 9, mango 4. Which flavour do girls like more?
quiz.explain: Girls: rose 9 > mango 4.

quiz.q: Boys: rose 5, mango 7. Girls: rose 9, mango 4. Which flavour sold more in total?
quiz.explain: Rose: 5 + 9 = 14. Mango: 7 + 4 = 11. Rose sold more.

teach.ask: Gappu's gola chart has 🍧 = 2. The mango row has 6 symbols. Gappu says 6 mango golas were sold. Help!
teach.praise: Each symbol is 2 golas, so 6 × 2 = 12 mango golas!
teach.nudge: What does the key tell you about each symbol?

learn.hook: Can a picture of one star stand for 5 children? In a pictograph it can!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how much one symbol stands for, like ⭐ = 5 children.
To read a row, multiply the number of symbols by the key value.
Half a symbol stands for half the key value. If ⭐ = 4, half a star = 2.
To draw a row, divide the number by the key value to find how many symbols.

example.q: Key: each ⭐ = 5 children. The cricket row has 4 stars. How many children like cricket?

learn.reallife: Newspapers and school notice boards use pictographs to show data in a fun way.

items.q: Key 🌟 = 4. Row has 2 and a half 🌟

items.text: Key 🪁 = 5 kites. To show 25 kites, draw ___ symbols.
Key 🚌 = 10 children. To show 40 children, draw ___ symbols.
Key 🍪 = 4 cookies. To show 12 cookies, draw ___ symbols.
Key ⭐ = 2 votes. Half a star stands for ___ vote.

quiz.q: Key: each ⭐ = 5 children. The cricket row has 4 stars. How many children like cricket?
quiz.explain: 4 stars × 5 children = 20 children.
quiz.mistake: Counts the stars but forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: each ⚽ = 10 children. The football row has 3 balls. How many children like football?
quiz.explain: 3 × 10 = 30 children.
quiz.mistake: Adds the key value instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Key: each 🪁 = 5 kites. A shop sold 25 kites. How many kite symbols should the row have?
quiz.explain: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for every kite

quiz.q: Key: each 🍪 = 4 cookies. A row shows 3 full cookies and half a cookie. How many cookies is that?
quiz.explain: 3 full symbols = 3 × 4 = 12. Half a symbol = 2. 12 + 2 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half symbol, or counts it as a full one

quiz.q: Key: each 📚 = 10 books. Monday has 2 symbols and Tuesday has 5 symbols. How many more books were borrowed on Tuesday?
quiz.explain: Tuesday has 5 - 2 = 3 more symbols. 3 × 10 = 30 more books.
quiz.mistake: Gives the difference in symbols (3) instead of books

quiz.q: Why does a pictograph need a key?
options: To tell how much one symbol stands for
quiz.explain: The key tells us the value of one symbol, so we can read the numbers.

quiz.q: Key: each 🚌 = 10 children. How should 40 children be shown?
quiz.explain: 40 ÷ 10 = 4, so draw 4 bus symbols.
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for each child

quiz.q: Key: each 😊 = 3 children. Class A has 4 symbols and Class B has 6 symbols. How many children are there in both classes?
quiz.explain: 4 + 6 = 10 symbols. 10 × 3 = 30 children.
quiz.mistake: Counts symbols without using the key

teach.ask: Gappu sees a pictograph with 5 apple pictures but the key says 🍎 = 2 apples. Gappu says 5 apples. Is that right?
teach.praise: Thanks! Each picture is 2 apples, so 5 × 2 = 10 apples. Always read the key!
teach.nudge: What does the key tell Gappu about each apple picture?

topics.title: Chess or cricket? A survey with two choices

learn.hook: Some children play only chess, some only cricket, some both and some neither. How do we sort them?
points: Ask each child two questions: Do you play chess? Do you play cricket?
Sort answers into 4 groups: only chess, only cricket, both, neither.
Record the counts in a table.
Children who play chess = only chess + both. Children who play cricket = only cricket + both.

example.q: Only chess 6, only cricket 10, both 4, neither 3. How many play cricket?

learn.reallife: Schools use surveys like this to plan clubs and sports periods.

games.title: Which group?
items: Chess club member who never plays cricket
Cricket team captain who also plays chess
Bowler who does not play chess

games.title: Survey table: only chess 6, only cricket 10, both 4, neither 3

quiz.q: Survey: only chess 6, only cricket 10, both 4, neither 3. How many play chess?
quiz.explain: Chess players = only chess + both = 6 + 4 = 10.

quiz.q: Same survey. How many play cricket?
Same survey. How many children were asked in all?
Same survey. Do more children play chess or cricket?
quiz.explain: Cricket 14 > chess 10.

quiz.q: Same survey. How many play both games?
quiz.explain: The table shows 4 in the 'both' group.

quiz.q: Sunil plays cricket and chess. In which group should he be recorded?
quiz.explain: He plays both games.

quiz.q: A child plays neither game. Which group?
quiz.explain: Neither means plays none of the two.

quiz.q: Same survey. How many play only one of the two games?
quiz.explain: Only chess 6 + only cricket 10 = 16.

teach.ask: Gappu surveyed friends about chess and cricket. Some play both! How should Gappu record and count?
teach.praise: Four groups: only chess, only cricket, both, neither. For cricket players, I add only cricket and both!
teach.nudge: Which groups do you need, and how do you count all the cricket players?

topics.title: Bal Mela: reading sales over days

learn.hook: At the school Bal Mela, popcorn and balloons sold out fast. Which day was the busiest?
points: A pictograph can show sales on different days. Read each day's row using the key.
Total for an item = add all its days. Total for a day = add all items on that day.
The day with the most sales has the biggest total.
Always check the key first: 🍿 = 10 packets means 3 symbols = 30 packets.

example.q: Using the popcorn pictograph (🍿 = 10), how many packets were sold over the three days?

learn.reallife: Organisers of fairs and melas count sales each day to plan stock and stalls for the next year.

games.title: Popcorn chart (🍿 = 10): Mon 3, Tue 5, Wed 4 symbols
Balloon chart (🎈 = 5): Mon 4, Tue 3, Wed 6 symbols
items: Tuesday sold more balloons than Monday.

quiz.q: Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. How many packets were sold on Tuesday?
quiz.explain: 5 symbols × 10 = 50.

quiz.q: Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. On which day were the most packets sold?
quiz.explain: Tuesday has the most symbols (5).

quiz.q: Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. How many packets were sold in all?
Bal Mela balloons sold (key 🎈 = 5). Mon: 🎈🎈🎈🎈 | Tue: 🎈🎈🎈 | Wed: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. How many balloons were sold on Wednesday?
Bal Mela balloons sold (key 🎈 = 5). Mon: 🎈🎈🎈🎈 | Tue: 🎈🎈🎈 | Wed: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. How many balloons were sold in all?
Popcorn (🍿 = 10): Mon 3, Tue 5, Wed 4. Balloons (🎈 = 5): Mon 4, Tue 3, Wed 6. What were Monday's total sales of both items?
quiz.explain: Popcorn 30 + balloons 20 = 50.

quiz.q: Using the same charts, which day had the biggest total sales of both items?
quiz.explain: Mon 30 + 20 = 50. Tue 50 + 15 = 65. Wed 40 + 30 = 70. Wednesday is highest.

quiz.q: Why should you check the key before reading a pictograph?
options: Each symbol may stand for more than 1
quiz.explain: If 🍿 = 10, then 3 symbols mean 30, not 3.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the busiest day at the Bal Mela. How should Gappu use the pictographs?
teach.praise: Use the key, add both items for each day, and the biggest total is the busiest day!
teach.nudge: How do you find each day's total, and then the busiest day?

topics.title: Bal Mela: comparing items and completing tables

learn.hook: On Wednesday, 40 popcorn packets and 30 balloons were sold. Which sold more, and by how much?
points: To compare two items on the same day, subtract the smaller number from the bigger one.
To complete a table from a pictograph, read each row with the key and write the number.
Check the table: the totals in the table must match the pictograph.
A completed table makes it easy to answer questions quickly.

example.q: On Tuesday, popcorn 50 packets and balloons 15. How many more popcorn packets?

learn.reallife: After a mela, teachers make a table of all sales to report to the principal.

games.title: Fill the table: popcorn 🍿 = 10 (Mon 3, Tue 5, Wed 4 symbols), balloons 🎈 = 5 (Mon 4, Tue 3 symbols)
Comparing on the same day
items: On Monday, popcorn (30) sold 10 more than balloons (20).
On Tuesday, balloons sold more than popcorn.
On Wednesday, popcorn sold 10 more than balloons.
To compare two items, we add them.
We subtract to find how many more.
A table must match the pictograph.

quiz.q: On Tuesday, popcorn sold 50 packets and balloons 15. How many more popcorn packets than balloons?
On Monday, popcorn 30 and balloons 20. How many more popcorn?
Bal Mela balloons sold (key 🎈 = 5). Mon: 🎈🎈🎈🎈 | Tue: 🎈🎈🎈 | Wed: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. Fill the table: balloons sold on Monday = ?
quiz.explain: 4 symbols × 5 = 20.

quiz.q: Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. Fill the table: popcorn sold on Wednesday = ?
A table says bangles: Mon 25, Tue 40, Wed 35. Key 💍 = 5. How many symbols for Tuesday?
quiz.explain: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 symbols.

quiz.q: Bangles: Mon 25, Tue 40, Wed 35. Key 💍 = 5. How many symbols for Monday?
On Wednesday, balloons 30, bangles 35. How many more bangles?
A table shows popcorn total 120 but the pictograph shows 3 + 5 + 4 symbols with 🍿 = 10. Is the table right?
quiz.explain: 12 symbols × 10 = 120, so the table matches.

teach.ask: Gappu has to fill a table from the Bal Mela pictograph and compare items. Explain how.
teach.praise: Multiply symbols by the key to fill the table, then subtract to compare. Done!
